The finding priced it as "more honest but costs a tape-format change", and the counted answer is that the tape-format change costs nothing: the mouse decoder is already `decodeIfPresent(...) ?? default` behind a `validateKeys` optional list, no checked-in fixture needs regenerating (the only two tapes with mouse events are decode-only libvterm fixtures; the danterm fixture tree has zero), `integrations/danterm/SKILL.md` does not document the mouse record keys, and the whole delta over option B is about twelve lines in three files the refactor already opens plus one new test. Against that dozen lines, option B does not merely leave "a value that claims a measurement it never made" -- it leaves a live divergence, because `PaneReplica#applyEvent` on iOS feeds tape mouse events straight into `applyNeutralTerminalMouse`, so the same off-grid Cmd-press that arms nothing on the Mac would arm a link on the phone replica, and no test in the tree would notice. The AGENTS.md bar asks for the structure in which the problem cannot happen, and the whole point of INTERACT-2 is that insideness must travel with the coordinates rather than be reconstructed downstream; option B reintroduces exactly that reconstruction one layer further out, in the one place the audit's own Correction already identifies as a real second producer. The purer variant -- record the raw point and cell size and re-derive insideness at replay, so the bit is never stored at all -- is worth naming and rejecting: the neutral schema is deliberately geometry-normalized so a tape can replay at a different grid, and carrying point-space would break that, which is why a recorded bit plus the surviving `isViewportPosition` range test is the right pair here.

### [MODEL-2](#model-2) -- Make SidebarItemStore reject nothing, or report rejection, so a dropped row op cannot strand the outline

**The question.** When SidebarItemStore refuses a row op, should the sweep repair the outline immediately with a full rebuild, or should the driver just decline to advance its projection cache and leave the repair to whatever sweep comes next?

**Option 1: Same-sweep reloadAll (`.rejected` reported up to the view)**

- _Shape._ `SidebarOutlineMutation` gains `case rejected` and every guard exit in `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/SidebarItemStore.swift#SidebarItemStore.apply(_:projection:)` returns it instead of `.none`; `.none` then has no producer and is deleted. `app/SidebarView.swift#applyRowOp` gains a `.rejected` arm and must tell its caller, so it stops being `-> Void` (an `inout Bool didReject`, or a small returned enum). `app/SidebarView.swift#applySidebarOps` widens to `-> (tabs: Set<TabId>, groups: Set<GroupId>, rejected: Bool)`, breaks out of the op loop on the first rejection, and runs `store.apply(.reloadAll, projection:)` plus `rebuildAllRows(groupCollapseStates:)` before the selection-restore block. `app/SidebarReconcileDriver.swift#reconcile` reads the third field and, on a rejected sweep, sets `appliedProjection = newProjection` directly, skipping `advanceSidebarCache` entirely because a full rebuild painted every row from `newProjection`.
- _Cost._ Three production files change substantively and one test file does. I counted by grepping app/, lib/, and tests-ui/ for `SidebarOutlineMutation`, `applySidebarOps`, `SidebarReconcileResult`, and `store.apply(`; the only non-TerminalCore hits are `SidebarItemStore.swift`, `SidebarView.swift` (two sites: `#applyRowOp` line-for-line, `#applySidebarOps` signature plus repair block), `SidebarReconcileDriver.swift` (the cache-advance assignment plus an optional `didReloadAll` field on `SidebarReconcileResult`), and `SidebarItemStoreTests.swift`. Correction to the starter kit: `SidebarItemStore.swift` has ten `return .none` statements, not fourteen (`grep -c "return .none"`) -- one each in `.insertGroup`, `.removeGroup`, `.reloadGroup`, `.setGroupCollapsed`, `.reloadTab`, three in `.insertTab`, two in `.removeTab`. All ten are mechanical one-word edits. Test churn: `SidebarItemStoreTests.swift#rejectedRowOpsReturnNoneWithoutChangingStore` (one test, fourteen `#expect` pairs across its twelve-op and two-op tables) plus the file-private `isNoOutlineMutation` helper; one new store test that a refused op returns `.rejected`; optionally one tests-ui test asserting the escalation. `tests-ui/SidebarTestSupport.swift` only forwards `SidebarReconcileResult` by name, so adding a field to it is source-compatible and costs nothing there.
- _Buys._ A rejection can no longer outlive the sweep that caused it, and `.none` -- the value that means both "nothing to do" and "I refused and told nobody" -- stops existing. It also fixes the second-order hazard neither the finding nor the decision states: row-op indices are cumulative (`Projections.swift#computeSidebarRowOps` documents "each index is relative to the running (intermediate) state"), so after a dropped op every later index is wrong, and `applyRowOp` hands those indices straight to `NSOutlineView.insertItems(at:inParent:)`. Aborting the loop turns a possible out-of-range AppKit exception into a rebuild.
- _Loses._ One flicker: a rejected sweep replaces animated insert/remove with `reloadData()`, losing the outline's animation and forcing the selection restore to run against fresh rows (it already does -- `applySidebarOps` snapshots `priorSelectedTabIds` before the loop and restores after it). The driver also has to pick one cache rule and write it down; assigning `newProjection` and skipping `advanceSidebarCache` discards that pass's rename-suppression and unapplied-attribute retention, which is correct after a rebuild but is a real semantic the code currently always applies.
- _Forecloses._ Nothing. `Conflicts with` names RECON-4 (key the sidebar projection's tabs by id), which rewrites `SidebarProjection` and touches the same three files -- it is a do-not-overlap conflict, not an ordering one, and it is wave 3. MODEL-4 also edits `computeSidebarRowOps` and `advanceSidebarCache` (wave 4), again same-file only. CHROME-2's recorded `after MODEL-2` edge is already corrected elsewhere in the audit to point at MODEL-1, not this finding. This road makes RECON-4 marginally easier, because the keyed-lookup rewrite lands on an `apply` whose failure paths all say the same word.

**Option 2: Driver declines to advance the cache; next sweep repairs**

- _Shape._ Identical to the option above through the whole store and view: `case rejected`, ten guard edits, a `.rejected` arm in `#applyRowOp`, the same widened `#applySidebarOps` return. The only difference is the tail -- `app/SidebarReconcileDriver.swift#reconcile` skips the `appliedProjection = advancedProjection` assignment on a rejected sweep so the stale cache re-diffs next time, and `#applySidebarOps` has no repair block.
- _Cost._ The same three production files and the same one test file. This is the load-bearing number: the saving over same-sweep repair is roughly ten to fifteen lines (the reloadAll repair block) and one line in the driver. Everything expensive about this work -- the enum case, the ten guard edits, threading rejection out of a Void function, widening the `applySidebarOps` tuple, rewriting the fourteen `.none` assertions and the `isNoOutlineMutation` helper -- is common to both roads and is not avoided here. And the loop abort is still required: without it the sweep keeps feeding stale cumulative indices to `NSOutlineView`, so this road does not even save that.
- _Buys._ Nothing structural. It is the same invariant as the option above, minus the repair, and it is about ten lines less work.
- _Loses._ The outline stays visibly wrong for an unbounded interval. Nothing schedules a sweep on the strength of a stale cache; coalesced sweeps arrive up to 75ms apart and do not arrive at all if the model stops changing. A user who closes the last tab of a group and then touches nothing sees the wrong rows until the next unrelated event. It also cannot be tested end to end: a tests-ui test can assert that a rejection happened, but there is no observable moment where the outline becomes correct again, so the repair itself has no test.
- _Forecloses._ Same as the option above -- nothing. But it leaves the escalation policy question open rather than answered, so RECON-4 or MODEL-4 lands on code whose repair semantics are still undecided, and whoever revisits it pays the ten lines then instead of now.

**Option 3: Store repairs itself; delete `.none` entirely** **&larr; recommended**

- _Shape._ No new enum case and no signature change anywhere in app/. Each of the ten guard failures in `SidebarItemStore.apply(_:projection:)` calls the existing private `#rebuildAllRows(projection:)` and returns `.reloadAll(groupCollapseStates:)` -- the arm the `.reloadAll` op already builds, factored into one helper. `case none` loses its last producer and is deleted from `SidebarOutlineMutation`. In `app/SidebarView.swift#applyRowOp` the `case .none: return` arm goes away and the function reports "this was a rebuild, stop" so `#applySidebarOps` breaks out of the loop; `.reloadAll` is already terminal in practice, since `computeSidebarRowOps` only ever emits it as the sole op. `app/SidebarReconcileDriver.swift` is untouched.
- _Cost._ Two production files change substantively, one is untouched, one test file changes. `SidebarItemStore.swift`: ten guard exits plus deleting one enum case plus one extracted helper. `SidebarView.swift`: one deleted arm and one small loop-abort signal -- no tuple widening, no `inout Bool`. `SidebarReconcileDriver.swift`: zero. Test churn is larger inside the one file than the other roads: `#rejectedRowOpsReturnNoneWithoutChangingStore` inverts rather than adjusts, because its premise (`sidebarStoreSnapshot(store) == before` after each refused op, asserted fourteen times) becomes false by design -- the store now equals the projection afterwards. `isNoOutlineMutation` is deleted in favour of a `requireReloadAll` in the same file-private style the other helpers use (`SidebarOutlineMutation` is not Equatable, since it carries the `SidebarItem` class, so it must stay a pattern-match helper).
- _Buys._ The strongest by-construction result of the three, and the one AGENTS.md asks for: after it, `SidebarOutlineMutation` has no value meaning "I did nothing". A caller cannot forget to handle rejection, because rejection is not a case it can pattern-match past -- it arrives as a rebuild the view already knows how to execute. There is no escalation policy to decide, no rejection flag to thread through two function signatures, and no way for the driver to advance its cache past a refusal, because the refusal already made the store match the projection. Same-sweep repair is not a rule someone has to obey; it is the only thing that can happen.
- _Loses._ Every refusal costs a full `reloadData()`, so the cost of a spurious rejection is much higher than under the other roads. That makes the shared prerequisite non-optional here: the `!new.isSingleGroupMode` gate plus the group-identity `reloadAll` in `Projections.swift#computeSidebarRowOps` must land first, or every single-group sweep that emits a group op (which the diff does unconditionally today, and the store refuses at `guard !projection.isSingleGroupMode`) rebuilds the whole outline instead of dropping the op harmlessly. It also gives up the explicit `.rejected` signal: a tests-ui test can no longer distinguish an escalation from a legitimate rebuild except by position in the script, so escalation observability lives in the core store tests rather than in `SidebarReconcileResult`.
- _Forecloses._ Nothing, and it slightly helps. RECON-4 rewrites `SidebarProjection` and edits `SidebarItemStore.apply`'s `projection.tab(_:)` lookups in `.insertTab` and `.reloadTab`; under this road those lookups have one uniform failure path instead of a second enum case to preserve. MODEL-4 (`computeSidebarRowOps` / `advanceSidebarCache` attribute grouping, wave 4) is untouched either way. The one thing it forecloses is adding a `rejected` field to `SidebarReconcileResult` later without re-introducing the plumbing this road deletes -- which is only a cost if a UI test genuinely needs to see the escalation.

**Recommendation: Store repairs itself; delete `.none` entirely.** The decision as framed assumes the cheap road is cheap, and counting says it is not: both `.rejected` roads touch the same three production files and the same test file, and the only thing "don't advance the cache" saves is about ten lines, while giving up bounded repair and any end-to-end test of it. So the honest comparison is not cheap-versus-correct; it is two same-priced roads where one leaves the outline wrong for an unbounded interval. Against that, the self-repair road is both the smaller change (two files, and the driver untouched) and the one that satisfies the AGENTS.md bar: it removes `.none`, the value that conflates "no work" with "I refused silently", so the failure the finding describes stops being expressible rather than becoming reportable. Its one real cost -- a refusal now buys a full `reloadData()` -- is paid only if refusals can happen spuriously, and the single known spurious refusal is exactly what the shared prerequisite removes: gate the group-level `sidebarSequenceOps` call on `!new.isSingleGroupMode` and emit `reloadAll` when the lone group's id changes. That half is already unblocked, carries the failing test, and should land as its own commit first under any of the three roads. If you want the escalation to be visible to a tests-ui assertion rather than only to the core store tests, take the same-sweep `.rejected` road instead -- it buys observability for roughly one extra file of plumbing, and that is the only thing it buys.

### [MODEL-5](#model-5) -- Move per-pane search and notification-throttle state into PaneModel so pane teardown prunes them

**The question.** Should per-pane search and notification-throttle state move into the pane tree (onto `PaneModel`, flat or behind a nested live bucket), or stay in `AppModel`'s two `[PaneId: ...]` dictionaries with the prune derived once per message instead of pushed from five teardown sites?

**Option 1: Flat fields on PaneModel**

- _Shape._ `AppModel.searchState` and `AppModel.lastNotificationTime` are deleted. `PaneModel` gains `var search: SearchModel? = nil` and `var lastNotification: [AlertKind: Date] = [:]`, both defaulted so all 151 `PaneModel(` construction sites keep compiling untouched. Every read becomes `model.pane(id)?.search` and every write becomes `model.updatePane(id) { $0.search = ... }` through the existing `AppModel.updatePane(_:_:)` / `AppModel.pane(_:)` pair. `Projections.swift#desiredSearchOverlays` changes from iterating a dictionary to walking `model.allPanes` and keying a pane iff `pane.search != nil`; `Projections.swift#desiredPaneFocus` reads through `pane(_:)`. `ModelOperations.swift#removePaneSearchState` is deleted and `ModelOperations.swift#clearPaneSideTables` shrinks to the `removeAlertsForPane` call alone.
- _Cost._ Counted with `grep -rn 'searchState|lastNotificationTime|clearPaneSideTables|removePaneSearchState' --include='*.swift' lib app ios`, then split into comment and non-comment lines and grouped by file. 128 matching lines total. Production: 4 files change substantively -- `Model.swift` (2 declarations plus a 2-line cross-domain comment), `ModelOperations.swift` (5), `Projections.swift` (2 code plus 2 doc-comment lines), `Update.swift` (24 non-comment, of which 5 are `clearPaneSideTables` calls that survive with narrowed meaning and 19 are real rewrites across the eight search arms and `throttledNotification`). One file is comment-only: `app/SwiftTerminalSessionView.swift` has a single stale mention. No `ios/` site at all. Tests: 9 files, 72 non-comment lines -- `UpdateSearchTests.swift` 27, `UpdateAlertTests.swift` 16, `TreeOwnsPanesTests.swift` 8, `ModelOperationsTests.swift` 7, `UpdateSessionEventTests.swift` 7, `DeterminismSeamTests.swift` 3, `UpdatePaneTests.swift` 2, `ProjectionsTests.swift` 1, `CheckpointCaptureTests.swift` 1. Separately, `grep -rn 'PaneModel(' --include='*.swift' lib app ios` returns 151 sites; all are safe because the new fields carry defaults, so none of them counts as a change site.
- _Buys._ "A destroyed pane's search overlay or notification throttle outlives it" stops being expressible: the state has no storage independent of the leaf that owns the pane, so no future teardown path can forget to prune it. It also makes the state follow its pane for free through `swapPaneModels` and the move-pane paths, which today carry the whole `PaneModel` payload while the side tables ride along only because their key happens not to change. It retires two of the three pane-keyed side tables the tree-owns-panes ADR left behind.
- _Loses._ The convention is narrowed, not deleted. `AlertModel.paneId` is non-optional but `alerts` is one global ordered list, so it cannot move onto `PaneModel`: `clearPaneSideTables` and all five Update.swift call sites survive, and a teardown path that forgets the call still leaks that pane's alerts. Two behaviors narrow, both unreachable from the product: `.searchStarted` for a PaneId in no tree becomes a silent no-op (today it creates state), and the defensive `.sessionCreationFailed` fallback for an already-gone pane has nothing left to clear. `desiredSearchOverlays` goes from O(active searches) -- normally zero -- to O(panes) per sweep; the model-driven reconciliation design doc already licenses per-sweep tree walks, so this is a note not a hazard. Three tests lose their premise outright (`ModelOperationsTests#clearPaneSideTablesPrunesEveryPaneKeyedSideTable`, the two seed-and-assert-prune tests in `UpdateAlertTests.swift`, and the `TreeOwnsPanesTests.swift` sessionCreationFailed cascade): after the move their assertion is a tautology, so that independent test surface collapses into the existing tree-ownership tests. The `PaneModel`-equality risk the finding raises does not materialize -- `containerShapeNode` and `containerLayoutNode` reduce a leaf to `pane.id` and `desiredPaneToolbar` builds from named fields.
- _Forecloses._ Makes REDUCE-2 and REDUCE-5 easier and discharges clusters C3 and X7 in the recorded order: both add new write sites against exactly these two dictionaries, so doing this first means they are written once against the final location. Leaves the LOOKUP-1 question open rather than answering it -- `app/AppRuntime.swift#currentLightCheckpointProjection` compares `LightCheckpointProjection(snapshot: toSnapshot(model))` and `Persistence.swift#toPaneSnapshot` enumerates fields explicitly, so nothing breaks today, but when LOOKUP-1 arrives it must either split `PaneModel` then or keep routing through `toSnapshot`. Nothing else in the backlog is made harder.

**Option 2: Derived reconcile, dictionaries stay**

- _Shape._ `AppModel.searchState` and `AppModel.lastNotificationTime` stay exactly where they are. `ModelOperations.swift#clearPaneSideTables` and `#removePaneSearchState` are replaced by one `reconcilePaneSideTables(_ model: inout AppModel)` that computes `Set(model.allPaneIds)` once and filters both dictionaries plus `model.alerts` to it. That call joins `reconcileTabState`, `reconcileTodoPopover`, `reconcilePendingConfirmation` and `reconcileSidebarRenameTarget` in the `defer` block at the top of `Update.swift#update`. All five explicit teardown calls are deleted. No search or throttle arm changes at all.
- _Cost._ Counted the same way. Production: 2 files -- `ModelOperations.swift` (two functions, about 12 lines, replaced by one) and `Update.swift` (5 call-site lines deleted, 1 defer line added, 2 adjacent comment lines reworded). `Model.swift` and `Projections.swift` are untouched. Tests: 1 file -- `ModelOperationsTests.swift#clearPaneSideTablesPrunesEveryPaneKeyedSideTable` (7 non-comment lines) must be re-expressed against the reconcile, plus one new behavioral test that closing a pane leaves no key. The other 8 test files and their 65 non-comment lines compile and pass unchanged, because the storage location does not move. Roughly one eighth the edit of the other two options.
- _Buys._ It deletes the five-call-site convention outright, and it covers all three side tables including `alerts`, which neither of the other options can. So on the narrow question "can a teardown path forget to prune", this option actually answers more of it than the stated ideal does. What it does not buy is structure: the state is still stored outside the tree that owns panes, so the invariant is repaired promptly rather than made unrepresentable.
- _Loses._ A stale entry is representable for the duration of one message -- any projection or helper called inside `update()` after the pane leaves the tree and before the `defer` fires reads it. It keeps the `[PaneId: X]` dual-ownership shape that the tree-owns-panes refactor removed for panes themselves, and keeps `Model.swift#AppModel`'s pane-access section header ('NO stored index is kept') in tension with two stored pane-keyed indexes. It also adds a full `Set(model.allPaneIds)` tree walk plus two dictionary filters to every single message, which cuts against LOOKUP-1's whole goal of making per-message work cheap; `reconcileTabState` guards itself with a `tabStateIsCanonical` early return, so this reconcile would want a comparable cheap gate to be honest about the same standard.
- _Forecloses._ Does not discharge C3 or X7. MODEL-5 stays open, so REDUCE-2's new `.startSearch` write site and REDUCE-5's `raiseAlert` funnel are still written against a location a later MODEL-5 would move -- the rework hazard the cluster names is deferred, not removed. It is the option most compatible with LOOKUP-1 as originally stated, but that compatibility is worth less than it looks: LOOKUP-1's own verifier already corrected the flat `groups` compare, because `SessionModel.progress`, `processPhase`, `command`, `agent` and `PaneTree.isZoomed` live inside `groups` and are not persisted, so LOOKUP-1 must cut through `PaneModel` and `SessionModel` regardless. It does sit well with REDUCE-3, which independently proposes adding `reconcileFocusedPaneAlerts` to the same `defer` block.

**Option 3: Nested live bucket on PaneModel** **&larr; recommended**

- _Shape._ Same move as option one, but the two fields land inside one nested value: `struct PaneLiveState: Equatable { var search: SearchModel? = nil; var lastNotification: [AlertKind: Date] = [:] }` and `PaneModel` gains `var live: PaneLiveState = .init()` beside its persisted `theme`, `fontSizeSteps`, `gridOverride` and `todos`. Reads become `model.pane(id)?.live.search`; writes become `model.updatePane(id) { $0.live.search = ... }`. `Persistence.swift#toPaneSnapshot` keeps enumerating fields and simply never reads `live`, so nothing about persistence changes today.
- _Cost._ Identical file and line counts to option one -- 4 production files and 33 non-comment production lines, 9 test files and 72 non-comment test lines, 151 `PaneModel(` sites still untouched because `live` is defaulted. The only difference is one extra member hop on lines that are already being rewritten, so the marginal cost over option one is close to zero. The real added cost is a design decision made earlier than it strictly has to be: naming and scoping the live bucket before LOOKUP-1 is planned.
- _Buys._ Everything option one buys, plus it turns the stated blocker into a down payment. LOOKUP-1's corrected fix requires a persisted half and a live half inside `PaneModel` anyway; this change creates that seam and puts the first two fields in it, so LOOKUP-1 later moves `SessionModel`'s live fields into the same shape rather than inventing it. It also makes the twelve `// ephemeral -- excluded from snapshots` line comments start becoming a type at the pane level, which is exactly the class of bug LOOKUP-1 exists to retire: a new live field cannot accidentally be picked up by a persisted-half comparison.
- _Loses._ Same losses as option one: `alerts` still needs `clearPaneSideTables` at five sites, the same two unreachable behaviors narrow, the same three tests lose their premise, and `desiredSearchOverlays` becomes an O(panes) walk. Added risk on top: it commits to a bucket name and boundary ahead of the finding that will use it, and LOOKUP-1's stated ideal has already been corrected once by its verifier -- so if the eventual split lands on a different shape (for example one nested value per snapshot concern rather than one live bucket), this is a small rename to redo. Both fields are unambiguously live under any reading of `toPaneSnapshot`, so the chance of putting the wrong field in the bucket is low.
- _Forecloses._ Same as option one for REDUCE-2 and REDUCE-5 -- clusters C3 and X7 are discharged and both become easier. Unlike option one, it makes LOOKUP-1 strictly easier rather than leaving it a question: the pane-level seam exists and `toSnapshot` is already field-enumerated, so LOOKUP-1's remaining work at the pane is to move the session's live fields in and point the comparison at the persisted half. It forecloses nothing in the backlog. MODEL-6, REDUCE-6 and the other Update.swift findings touch different structures.

**Recommendation: Nested live bucket on PaneModel.** The stated blocker for this finding is mostly already gone. LOOKUP-1's original "compare `groups` wholesale" idea was corrected by its own verifier because `SessionModel.progress`, `processPhase`, `command`, `agent` and `PaneTree.isZoomed` already sit inside `groups` and are not persisted -- so LOOKUP-1 must split persisted from live *inside* `PaneModel` and `SessionModel` no matter what MODEL-5 does. Live search state is not what breaks the fast compare; session churn already did. Given that, the nested bucket costs the same as the flat move (identical 4 production files, identical 9 test files, identical 72 non-comment test lines -- the only delta is one `.live` hop on lines that are being rewritten anyway) and it lands the seam LOOKUP-1 needs instead of adding to LOOKUP-1's bill. It is also the option the AGENTS.md bar picks: a destroyed pane's search overlay or throttle entry stops being expressible, rather than being repaired promptly. The honest number the owner is trading against: the reconcile fallback is roughly one eighth the edit (2 production files, ~8 production lines, 1 test rewritten, every other test compiles untouched) and it actually retires *more* of the convention, because `AlertModel.paneId` is non-optional so one reconcile can prune alerts too -- which the ideal cannot, leaving `clearPaneSideTables` and all five call sites alive for the alert feed. If the owner takes the fallback, the right follow-up is to say so in the plan: the tree-owns-panes invariant then stops at panes and does not extend to their live state, and MODEL-5 stays open ahead of REDUCE-2 and REDUCE-5.

### [RUNTIME-2](#runtime-2) -- Give the theme browser a model slot so `reconcileThemeBrowser` owns its existence

**The question.** When the theme browser's existence becomes a model slot, does the sweep repair pane focus on the close transition -- move `reconcileThemeBrowser()` above `reconcilePaneFocus()` -- or does it leave the pass where it is and let focus recover on some later sweep?

**Option 1: Browser pass moves above pane focus** **&larr; recommended**

- _Shape._ The sweep in `app/Reconcile.swift#reconcile` gains one moved line: `reconcileThemeBrowser()` sits between `reconcilePaneChrome(tally:)` and `reconcilePaneFocus()`, with a comment stating the rule ("a pass that destroys a focused view runs before the focus repair"). Everything else is the lift itself: `AppModel.themeBrowserOpen: Bool`, `Msg.toggleThemeBrowser`, `desiredThemeBrowser(in: AppModel) -> ThemeBrowserProjection?` gated on the flag, and `reconcileThemeBrowser()` creating/inserting/constraining the view on nil -> non-nil and calling `removeFromSuperview()` on the reverse, on the `Reconcile.swift#reconcileAlertsPopover` template. The pass stays after `reconcileContainers()`, so `AppRuntime#buildAndInsertContainer`'s `positioned: .below, relativeTo: browser` z-order still holds.
- _Cost._ Zero files beyond the lift; one line moved plus one comment. The lift itself (identical under every option) is 8 production files and 4 test files, counted by grepping `toggleThemeBrowser`, `themeBrowserView`, `desiredThemeBrowser`, and `ThemeBrowserProjection` across app/, lib/, app-tests/, tests-ui/. Substantive: `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Model.swift#AppModel`, `.../Update.swift#update`, `.../Projections.swift#desiredThemeBrowser`, `app/Reconcile.swift#reconcileThemeBrowser` (~20-line rewrite), `app/AppRuntime.swift#toggleThemeBrowser` (22 lines deleted, field comment retitled). Signature/one-line only: `.../Msg.swift#Msg`, `app/AppDelegate.swift#toggleThemeBrowser(_:)`, `app/ThemeBrowserView.swift#closeBrowser`. Tests: 6 `desiredThemeBrowser` call sites lose their non-optional shape (5 across 3 tests in `lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/ProjectionsTests.swift`, 1 in the `tests-ui/ThemeBrowserViewTests.swift` fixture); 1 of the 26 `uiTest`s in `tests-ui/ThemeBrowserViewTests.swift` inverts ("close button calls toggleThemeBrowser"); 2 lines delete from `tests-ui/SidebarViewTestShim.swift` (`themeBrowserToggles`, the shim `toggleThemeBrowser()`); 1 new app-tests file. Verification caveat that costs this option, not the others: the focus half cannot be asserted in the gate. `reconcilePaneFocus` needs `AppRuntime.window`, and `NSWindow(` appears 10+ times in tests-ui and zero times in app-tests, while tests-ui cannot compile `app/Reconcile.swift`. Live check instead: open a slot, toggle the browser, and read `danterm --socket <s> focus` (`IpcRequestMethod.focusInfo` -> `PaneFocusReconciliation#paneFocusInfoResult`).
- _Buys._ Keeps today's behavior exactly: close the browser, the terminal takes the keyboard back in the same send frame. It also makes the sweep obey the rule `docs/design/2026-05-27-model-driven-view-reconciliation.md` already states -- passes that destroy hosts run before passes that render into them -- rather than leaving the theme browser as an exception to it. No new bug class is retired beyond the lift's own "the browser is on screen but the model does not know it".
- _Loses._ Nothing behavioral. The one thing to confirm (and I did, by reading): no pass between `reconcilePaneChrome` and `reconcileThemeBrowser`'s new position reads `themeBrowserView` or `contentArea`; only `buildAndInsertContainer` reads the field, and it runs inside `reconcileContainers()`, still first. On the open transition nothing in `ThemeBrowserView` calls `makeFirstResponder` during construction, so the later `reconcilePaneFocus()` sees the terminal as claimant and no-ops -- opening still does not steal focus. Residual risk is the same z-order note the finding already names.
- _Forecloses._ Nothing. CHROME-5 ("needs the theme browser's model slot", wave 3) is unblocked by the lift regardless of ordering. REDUCE-4 adds a `reconcileSessionFocus` pass beside `reconcilePaneFocus`; landing this ordering first gives that work a stated rule to place itself against instead of re-asking the same question. REDUCE-2 depends on `reconcilePaneChrome` running before `reconcilePaneFocus`, which this preserves.

**Option 2: Leave the pass last; focus recovers later**

- _Shape._ Identical code to the option above minus the moved line: `reconcileThemeBrowser()` stays between `reconcileTodoPopover()` and `syncPaneVisibility()`. On the close transition the pass removes the browser after `reconcilePaneFocus()` has already run, so nothing repairs the first responder inside that sweep.
- _Cost._ Cheapest by exactly one line and one comment; the 8 production / 4 test files above are unchanged. No new test is possible either, so the two options are indistinguishable on gate cost.
- _Buys._ Nothing structural. It is one line less work, and it avoids having to re-read the sweep to confirm the move is safe -- a confirmation this analysis already did.
- _Loses._ A live behavior the current code deliberately has. `AppRuntime#toggleThemeBrowser`'s close arm calls `reconcilePaneFocus()` on purpose: `removeFromSuperview()` on a view owning the first responder drops the window's responder to the window itself, which `PaneFocusReconciliation#paneFocusClaimant` classifies as `.none`, and the repair puts focus back on the terminal host. Under this option that repair waits for the next Msg from any source -- and on an idle shell prompt no Msg comes, because the keystrokes that would produce one are exactly what is being dropped. `reconcile()` has no periodic driver; `AppRuntime#dispatchInFrame` runs it per send, and a new payload-free `toggleThemeBrowser` case would return false from `Msg#coalescesReconcile`, so `.reconcileNow` applies but only when something sends. So this is a user-visible regression: browse themes, click Close, then type -- nothing happens until you click a pane. It also contradicts the ordering rule in `docs/design/2026-05-27-model-driven-view-reconciliation.md`. Papering over it with the outbox (the pass reports a Msg so a second sweep repairs focus) costs a Msg case, an update arm, and a whole extra sweep per close -- strictly worse than the one moved line.
- _Forecloses._ Makes REDUCE-4 harder in a small way: it leaves the sweep with an undocumented "focus repair may run before a view is destroyed" hole, so the new `reconcileSessionFocus` pass has to answer the same ordering question with no precedent. Nothing else in the backlog changes; CHROME-5 is unaffected.

**Option 3: Move reconcilePaneFocus last in the sweep**

- _Shape._ Instead of lifting the browser pass, drop `reconcilePaneFocus()` to the bottom of `Reconcile.swift#reconcile`, immediately before `syncPaneVisibility()`, so focus repair is the last thing after every view-existence pass -- containers, chrome, sidebar, switcher, confirmation, preferences, both popovers, and the theme browser. `reconcileThemeBrowser()` then stays where it is and still gets its repair.
- _Cost._ Also one moved line, and the same 8 production / 4 test files. It additionally requires editing the ordering paragraph in `docs/design/2026-05-27-model-driven-view-reconciliation.md` ("Pane-focus reconciliation runs after pane chrome" becomes "...runs last, after every existence pass"), so one doc file joins the change.
- _Buys._ The real invariant, and this is the AGENTS.md-ideal road: "a pass destroyed a focused view later in the sweep than the focus repair ran" stops being expressible for every pass at once, not just the theme browser. `reconcilePaneFocus` is already safe to run late by its own rules -- it returns early on a `.nonPane` claimant, so a sidebar rename field editor or any other deliberate non-pane owner is preserved, and it only acts when a pane claimant mismatches or nobody claims.
- _Loses._ It changes focus-repair ordering relative to `reconcileSidebar`, `reconcileSwitcher`, `reconcileConfirmation`, `reconcilePreferencesPanel`, `reconcileAlertsPopover`, and `reconcileTodoPopover` all at once, and no test in the gate can catch a regression there for the same reason as above: focus repair needs an `NSWindow`, which app-tests never construct and tests-ui cannot pair with the real runtime. It also widens a change whose stated scope is one panel, so a focus regression discovered later would be ambiguous between this reordering and the lift.
- _Forecloses._ Nothing negatively, and it makes REDUCE-4 easiest of the three: with "focus passes run last" stated, `reconcileSessionFocus` has an obvious home. Its natural moment is exactly REDUCE-4, when a second focus pass forces the rule to be written down anyway.

**Recommendation: Browser pass moves above pane focus.** Take the one-line move. This is the rare case where the cheap road and the correct road are the same price: option 2 saves one line and pays for it with a user-visible regression -- close the browser on an idle prompt and the keyboard goes nowhere, because the only thing that would trigger the repairing sweep is the keystrokes being dropped -- while the ordering rule it violates is already written in docs/design/2026-05-27-model-driven-view-reconciliation.md. So option 2 needs a justification it does not have. The honest note about the ideal is that option 3, not option 1, is the AGENTS.md ideal: putting reconcilePaneFocus last retires the whole class ("a pass destroyed a focused view after the focus repair ran") for every panel instead of fixing this one instance, and it costs the same single line plus a doc edit. I still recommend option 1 for RUNTIME-2 because option 3 silently changes focus ordering against six other passes that no headless test can cover -- app-tests never build an NSWindow and tests-ui cannot compile app/Reconcile.swift -- and mixing that into a change scoped to one panel makes any later focus regression ambiguous. Write option 3 into the plan as the named ideal and schedule it with REDUCE-4, which adds a second focus pass and therefore forces the "focus passes run last" rule to be stated anyway.

### [RUNTIME-3](#runtime-3) -- Stop opening nested modal run loops from inside an open send frame

**The question.** For RUNTIME-3, do we take only the demonstrated ordering fix (start the IPC accept loop after the launch prompt resolves), or do we also lift every user-visible alert out of the send frame -- and if we lift them, do we make them non-blocking sheets or fully model-projected panels?

**Option 1: IPC start ordering only (the cheap, demonstrated fix)**

- _Shape._ Split the accept loop out of `AppRuntime.swift#init`. The `IpcServer(socketPath:tailnetConfig:runtimeDispatch:)` construction and the `schedulingLifecycle.arm(.ipcServer)` stop token stay in `init` (so the control socket is still bound and claimed at launch and `IpcServerOwnershipTests` keeps passing), and only the `let startToken = schedulingLifecycle.arm(.deferredCallback)` plus `Task { await server?.start() }` block moves into a new `func startIpcServer()`. `app/AppDelegate.swift#applicationDidFinishLaunching` calls `runtime.startIpcServer()` after the restore-prompt branch resolves, on all three paths (init snapshot, prompt, fresh). Every alert keeps its `NSAlert.runModal()`.
- _Cost._ 2 production files, ~12 lines moved. 0 test files change. Counted by reading `AppRuntime.swift` init (lines around the `startsApplicationServices` IPC block), `AppRuntime.swift#stopIpcServer` (confirms only `ipcServerToken`/`ipcServer` are paired, both of which stay in init), and `app/IpcServer.swift` (`ControlSocketListener.open` runs in `init`, the accept loops run in `start()` -- so deferring `start()` defers acceptance without releasing socket ownership). `grep -rn "startsApplicationServices" app app-tests` shows all three app-test runtimes pass `false`, so none of them ever construct a server: no test compiles differently. One hidden cost if you want a real regression test: `AppRuntime.init` hardcodes `controlSocketPath()` with no injection point, so an end-to-end "no reply arrives before startIpcServer(), a reply arrives after" probe needs one extra defaulted socket-path parameter on `init`.
- _Buys._ Nothing structural. It removes the one window the audit actually demonstrated -- an IPC request served during `runModal` mutating a model that `commitRestoreSession` then overwrites with `model = staged.model` -- and it does so by ordering, not by construction. A future edit can put a `runModal` back inside a frame and nothing catches it.
- _Loses._ Loses nothing behavioral. The risk is that it is untestable as written: the audit's own starter kit says this step has no new failing test available in app-tests, so it lands as a pure ordering change under `IpcServerOwnershipTests` as characterization. It also leaves four live `presentAlert` call sites and the `.saveDanTermConfig` arm's in-frame `runModal` exactly as they are, so the finding's headline claim stays true after the fix ships.
- _Forecloses._ Forecloses nothing and unblocks the most. It is a strict prerequisite for both other roads, and it alone satisfies what C5 needs before RUNTIME-1: the discard C5 describes is an IPC-driven `update()` racing the prompt, and no acceptance means no race, so RUNTIME-1's `.sessionRestored(model:)` conversion can proceed on top of this without the projected-panel work. Watch the sequencing against RUNTIME-4, which re-owns every `schedulingLifecycle` handle/token pair including `.ipcServer` and the `.deferredCallback` start token this option relocates. Shallow textual overlap with PERSIST-2, which also edits `applicationDidFinishLaunching` to thread `RecoveryPaths`.

**Option 2: Non-blocking sheet port (keep the port, drop the nested loop)**

- _Shape._ `AppRuntimePorts.presentAlert` survives but stops nesting a run loop: `AppRuntimePorts.swift#live` builds the same `NSAlert` and ends with `alert.beginSheetModal(for: window) { _ in }` instead of `alert.runModal()`. The ports struct holds no window, so the signature gains one -- `var presentAlert: @MainActor (NSWindow?, String, String) -> Void` -- and the four call sites in `AppRuntime.swift` pass `window`. The model, `Msg`, `update()`, `Projections.swift`, and `Reconcile.swift` are untouched. The launch prompt in `AppDelegate` is not addressed by this at all, so Option 1's ordering split still ships alongside it.
- _Cost._ 3 production files, 4 test files unchanged. Counted from `grep -rn "presentAlert" --include="*.swift" app app-tests lib tests-ui` -- 7 hits in 3 files. Substantive: `app/AppRuntimePorts.swift` (declaration + `live` body), `app/AppRuntime.swift` (`presentConfigError`, `showImportError`, and the `let presentAlert = ports.presentAlert` capture in the `.exportState` arm each gain a window argument). Signature-only: `app-tests/AppRuntimeCommandTestSupport.swift#RecordingAppRuntimePorts` -- one closure parameter list. The three `#expect(ports.alerts...)` lines in `app-tests/AppRuntimeIpcCommandTests.swift` survive verbatim, because the recording port still records. Add Option 1's 2 files and ~12 lines for the launch prompt.
- _Buys._ Removes the nested run loop from every alert path with the smallest possible behavioral delta, and keeps the alert window-modal, so decision (2) evaporates -- nobody can miss a config write failure, and the owner does not have to rule on prominence. But it is not structural: `AppRuntimePorts` still exposes a synchronous void-returning port that a future `live` implementation could make blocking again, so "no command arm blocks the main actor" remains a convention, not a type.
- _Loses._ A sheet needs a window. `presentPendingConfigError()` runs right after `runtime.window = window` so it is fine, but any alert raised before the window exists (or in a headless/benchmark build) needs a defined fallback, and the obvious fallback is `runModal` -- which conditionally reintroduces exactly the hazard being removed. Also loses the synchronous ordering the `.saveDanTermConfig` arm currently has: the alert now appears after `send(.fontFamilyResolved(...))` rather than before it. No test can be written that says "no port call happens inside perform", because the port call still happens inside perform -- it just no longer blocks.
- _Forecloses._ Neutral-to-mildly-negative. It leaves `presentAlert` in `AppRuntimePorts`, so the later ideal has to unpick this window-threading change before deleting the port -- work done twice. It does nothing for RUNTIME-1/C5 by itself (the launch prompt is a bare `NSAlert` in `AppDelegate`, not a port call), so Option 1 is still required. It does not touch `PendingConfirmation`, so it stays clear of C2 (MODEL-1 + CHROME-2). It also does not build the seventh panel-projection pass, so RUNTIME-2's theme-browser model slot gets no help from it.

**Option 3: Model-projected notice panel (the ideal)** **&larr; recommended**

- _Shape._ `AppRuntimePorts.presentAlert` is deleted. `AppModel` gains an ephemeral slot beside `pendingConfirmation` -- note `AppModel.alerts` is already taken by the bell feed, so name it something else, e.g. `var pendingNotice: PendingNotice?`. `Msg` gains a report case and a dismiss case with their `update()` arms; `Projections.swift` gains `struct NoticeProjection: Equatable` and `func desiredNotice(in model: AppModel) -> NoticeProjection?`; `Reconcile.swift` gains a `caches.notice` field and a `reconcileNoticePanel()` pass modeled line-for-line on `reconcileConfirmation()`, driving a new `NoticePanel` (or a widened `ConfirmationPanel`). `AppRuntime.presentConfigError` and `showImportError` collapse to `send(.noticeReported(...))`, and the launch restore prompt in `AppDelegate` becomes a launch model slot whose Restore / Start Fresh buttons arrive as Msgs.
- _Cost._ 9 production files (8 edited + 1 new panel) and 5 test files. Counted site by site. `app/AppRuntime.swift`: 8 edit points -- `init` (server split), the `.saveDanTermConfig` arm, the `.exportState` arm's captured `presentAlert`, `presentConfigError`, `presentPendingConfigError`, `reloadDanTermConfig`, `openDanTermConfig`, `showImportError` (verified by `grep -n "presentConfigError\|showImportError" app/AppRuntime.swift`: 4 + 3 call sites plus 2 definitions). `app/AppRuntimePorts.swift`: 2 (declaration + `live`). `app/AppDelegate.swift`: 1 substantive (the prompt at the `let response = alert.runModal()` site). `app/Reconcile.swift`: 3 small (cache field, pass, call in `reconcile()`). Core: `Model.swift`, `Msg.swift`, `Update.swift`, `Projections.swift`. Plus one new panel file -- `app/ConfirmationPanel.swift` is 298 lines as the size reference, though a title/text/one-button notice is much smaller. Tests: `app-tests/AppRuntimeCommandTestSupport.swift` (delete `alerts` + the `presentAlert` closure -- 2 lines, but every app-test suite constructs this value, so it must land in the same commit), `app-tests/AppRuntimeIpcCommandTests.swift` (rewrite 3 assertions in "config save failure alerts..." onto the model slot, plus the new failing test), and new cases in the DanTermCore `ProjectionsTests`/`UpdateLifecycleTests` suites. `app-tests/AppRuntimeAmbientCommandTests.swift` needs no change -- I read its `.exportState` test and it only exercises the success path; `grep -rn "importState\|showImportError" app-tests` returns nothing, so the import path has no test to update either. Four suites are pure safety net and should not change: `AppRuntimePendingIpcShutdownTests`, `IpcServerOwnershipTests`, `IpcServerRemoteTests`, `AppRuntimeSchedulingLifecycleTests`.
- _Buys._ The port is gone, so "a command arm opens a nested run loop" stops being expressible from any alert path -- not avoided, not reviewed for, but absent from the type. The launch prompt stops being a modal at all, which retires the whole class where a request served during a prompt mutates a model the bootstrap then overwrites. It also collapses three ad-hoc alert helpers into one model slot with one projection, so all user-visible notices become pure-testable in DanTermCore instead of requiring a recording port in app-tests.
- _Loses._ The behavior change the audit flags: a config write failure becomes dismissible-later rather than must-dismiss-now. That is real, but smaller than it reads -- `reconcileConfirmation` already calls `center(on: window)` and `makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)` on the nil-to-non-nil transition, so the projected notice takes key focus on appear the same way the quit confirmation does. Risks: a single notice slot silently drops a second notice raised while the first is up (the existing `pendingConfirmation` has the same single-slot shape, so choose deliberately -- one slot or a queue). `scripts/reducer-command-discard-lint.sh` constrains how the report Msg is threaded from the `.saveDanTermConfig` catch arm. And the new test the audit wants -- "no port call happens inside perform" -- only proves the structural claim; it still does not ablate an actual `runModal`-nested IPC mutation, which the audit's own Correction admits was never reproduced.
- _Forecloses._ Best downstream position of the three, with one collision to avoid. Makes RUNTIME-1 easiest: C5's stated resolution is literally this option's first half, and with no modal anywhere in launch, `.sessionRestored(model:)` plus `private(set) var model` can land with no residual race. Makes RUNTIME-2 nearly free: it is the same "give it a model slot and a reconcile pass" template, so whoever writes the notice pass has just written RUNTIME-2's. The collision: do NOT implement the notice by adding subjects to `PendingConfirmation` or by widening `ConfirmationPanel`'s projection -- MODEL-1 and CHROME-2 (group C2) are jointly redesigning `PendingConfirmation` into a per-subject enum and replacing `confirmConfirmation`/`cancelConfirmation`/`chooseDeleteGroupConfirmation` with one `.answerConfirmation(id:answer:)`, and a notice subject dropped into that type would be rewritten twice. A separate `pendingNotice` slot with its own projection stays entirely out of C2's way. Shallow overlap with PERSIST-2 (also edits `applicationDidFinishLaunching`) and with RUNTIME-4 (also re-owns the `.ipcServer` / `.deferredCallback` scheduling tokens this option relocates).

**Recommendation: Model-projected notice panel (the ideal), with the IPC start split as its first commit.** The ideal costs roughly 5x the cheap road in files (9 production + 5 test versus 2 production + 0 test), and that is the number to trade against -- but three things make it cheaper than the audit implies. First, it is not new architecture: `ReconcilerCaches` already carries six single-optional panel projections (`confirmation`, `preferencesPanel`, `alertsPopover`, `todoPopover`, `themeBrowser`, `switcher`), each with the identical `desiredX(in: model)` / diff / lazily-create-panel shape, so the notice pass is the seventh copy of a template with six worked examples. Second, the compile blast radius that looks scary is not: only `app-tests/AppRuntimeCommandTestSupport.swift#RecordingAppRuntimePorts` constructs the ports value, and exactly one test (`AppRuntimeIpcCommandTests`, three `#expect` lines) asserts on `ports.alerts`. Third, the user-assent question in decision (2) is smaller than stated -- `Reconcile.swift#reconcileConfirmation` already calls `makeKeyAndOrderFront` on the nil-to-non-nil transition, so a projected notice takes key focus on appear and a config write failure is no easier to miss than the quit confirmation is. What the ideal buys that neither cheaper road does: `AppRuntimePorts` loses `presentAlert` entirely, so "a command arm blocks the main actor" stops being writable rather than merely being avoided by review, and the launch prompt stops being a modal at all -- which is what C5 asks for before RUNTIME-1 converts the restore commit into a Msg. The honest caveat, per AGENTS.md: split the work as the finding says. Commit one is the IPC start split (Option 1), which is a genuine prerequisite for both other roads, closes the only demonstrated race on its own, and unblocks RUNTIME-1 immediately -- so if the owner stops after commit one, nothing is wasted and the ideal stays on the table.

### [STORE-4](#store-4) -- State the open tail's scratch-table key base once, so a trimmed head cannot key it two ways

**The question.** For the open tail's scratch-table key base, do we introduce a one-field `OriginalCellOffset` type so a trimmed-relative count cannot be handed to a key-taking parameter, or do we just rebase the writer sites to the original base and state the base in a comment?

**Option 1: Typed OriginalCellOffset** **&larr; recommended**

- _Shape._ A frozen one-field `struct OriginalCellOffset` (private to `Terminal.LogicalLineStore`) becomes the type of `HyperlinkEntry.offset` and `IdentityRun.start`, and the parameter type of `hyperlinkId(record:at:keyOffset:)` and `contentIdentity(record:at:keyOffset:)`. `IdentityRun.extent` stays a plain `Int` -- it is a length, not an offset. One new private accessor, `openRecordKeyBase` (`headTrimmedCells` when the open record is also the head, 0 otherwise), is the only producer of the base, and `cell(recordIndex:recordOffset:record:cellOffset:)` becomes the single place where a retained-relative offset is converted into a key. `RecordTextPosition.cellOffset` keeps its `Int`, so the type never leaves the file.
- _Cost._ Twelve mandatory change sites, all in `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift`, all private: the new type; `#HyperlinkEntry`; `#IdentityRun`; the new `openRecordKeyBase`; `#appendCells` (three expressions -- the `cellOffset` computation, the run-continuation test `open.start + open.extent == cellOffset`, and the `IdentityRun` init); `#cutTail` (four comparisons against `newCellCount`); `#flushOpenTables` (two `setU16` writes plus the per-cell `run.start + step < record.cellCount` bound and the `identityEntryCount` sizing); `#loadOpenScratch` (two constructions plus the per-cell branch that uses the loop index, which is already original-base and must NOT be rebased); `#hyperlinkId`; `#contentIdentity`; `#cell(recordIndex:recordOffset:record:cellOffset:)`; `#forEachHyperlinkId`. Counted by grepping every use of `openHyperlinks`, `openIdentityRuns`, `keyOffset` and `headTrimmedCells` in the file and attributing each to its enclosing function. Zero test files change: `grep -c` for `headTrimmedCells|HyperlinkEntry|IdentityRun` in `TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift` returns 0, and nothing outside the store names those types. One new test (the starter kit's). The audit's "roughly seventeen" is this twelve plus five optional boundary sites -- `#recordTextPosition`, `#position(of:)`, `#contentRank`, `#independentContentRank`, `#closedContentUnitTotal`, and `ClosedRecordScan.cellOffsetBase` -- which only change if the type crosses into `RecordTextPosition`; that variant also drags in 21 lines of `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/TerminalSearch.swift` and puts a wrapper inside a coordinate whose two-word storage `recordCoordinateStaysTwoWords` asserts. Recommend not crossing.
- _Buys._ Handing a retained-relative cell index to a table keyed by original offsets stops compiling. The file converts `headTrimmedCells` by hand at nine sites (`#cell`, `#recordTextPosition`, `#position(of:)`, `#contentRank`, `#independentContentRank`, `#closedContentUnitTotal`, `#closedRecordScan`, `#forEachHyperlinkId`, and the `#recordsEqual` head-trim branch); the type makes eight of them unable to produce a key at all, leaving `#cell` as the one sanctioned crossing. It also forces a decision on two things the plain rebase can skip silently: `flushOpenTables` sizes the per-cell identity table by the trimmed `record.cellCount` while `contentIdentity` guards with `keyOffset < record.identityEntryCount`, so a record trimmed while open and then closed mis-sizes and mis-keys its per-cell table -- a second bug in the same family that the type surfaces as a compile error at the `setU32` index.
- _Loses._ Ceremony in the hottest read path in the store: `hyperlinkId` and `contentIdentity` run per cell inside borrowing reads, so the wrapper must be a frozen single-field struct with `Comparable` and a difference operator, and the plan must assert (per `docs/design/2026-07-29-cross-module-value-dispatch.md` and the doc-28/doc-16 history in `agent-docs/terminal-performance.md`) that it costs nothing at -O rather than assuming it. The type also cannot express the whole invariant on its own: `setU16` truncates silently (`UInt16(truncatingIfNeeded:)`) and `flushOpenTables` writes keys through it, so original-base keys on a trimmed-then-extended record can exceed the record's own cell count and the plan still owes an explicit bound or precondition there. Nothing behavioral is given up.
- _Forecloses._ Makes HIST-1 easier and STORE-3 consistent. HIST-1 is marked both "Do after STORE-4" and "Conflicts with STORE-4" and rewrites `#appendCells` and the close path to hold the open record's spills (and, in its larger half, its decoded header) in scratch; once `record.cellCount` inside `appendCells` is read through `openRecordKeyBase`, HIST-1 has one place to re-point instead of three raw expressions. STORE-3 introduces a one-type encode/decode wrapper for the 8-byte cell word in the same functions, so the same idiom lands twice rather than the file carrying two philosophies. STORE-1 (bytes-in-use at twelve sites) and STORE-5 (block record-range accessor) touch the same file but not these expressions. Nothing in the backlog becomes harder.

**Option 2: Rebase the three writer sites**

- _Shape._ No new type. `#appendCells` computes its key as `record.cellCount + index + openRecordKeyBase`; `#cutTail` compares against `newCellCount + openRecordKeyBase`; `#flushOpenTables` handles the trimmed-open-then-closed case for the per-cell table. `HyperlinkEntry.offset` and `IdentityRun.start` stay `Int` and gain a `///` line stating that they are original-base keys. The one private `openRecordKeyBase` accessor still gets added, because otherwise the base is spelled three more times. Drop the audit's `precondition` from this option -- see the risk column.
- _Cost._ Three functions plus one new accessor, all in `LogicalLineStore.swift`: `#appendCells`, `#cutTail`, `#flushOpenTables`, `#openRecordKeyBase`. `#loadOpenScratch` needs no edit (it already reads original-base keys out of the arena) but does need a comment saying so. Zero test files change; the same one new test. Counted the same way as option A -- every use of `openHyperlinks`/`openIdentityRuns` attributed to its enclosing function, then split into writers (three) and readers (five, all already original-base). Note the audit's "one-line fix to `appendCells`" undercounts: rebasing `appendCells` alone leaves `cutTail`'s trimmed-base bound filtering the wrong entries and leaves `flushOpenTables` writing original-base keys into a table sized by the trimmed cell count, so the cheap road is three sites, not one.
- _Buys._ Nothing structural. It fixes the one demonstrated key mismatch and states the base in prose. The nine hand-written base conversions stay, and the next reader who adds a lookup can still hand a retained-relative offset to a key parameter and get a silently wrong hyperlink id or content identity -- the same move that produced this finding.
- _Loses._ Only the invariant. No behavior is given up and no ADR is contradicted. The real hazard is in the variant this option is usually paired with: `precondition(headTrimmedCells == 0 || offsets.count > 1)` in `#trimHeadRecord` guards a reachable state. `#makeRoom` calls `evictOneDisplayRow()` when it cannot find a contiguous run, and with a single open record that trims the open head -- so the precondition turns a latent misattribution into a live trap in the terminal, and the starter kit's failing test (which drives exactly that state through `evictOneDisplayRow`) would trap instead of pass. Swift Testing cannot catch a `precondition` in-process, so the test would have to become an exit test. Take this option without the precondition, or not at all.
- _Forecloses._ Leaves HIST-1 to re-derive the base a second time when it moves the open record's header and spills into scratch, since `record.cellCount` stays spelled inline in `#appendCells` and the close path. Makes nothing moot: the nine conversion sites remain, so the typed shape stays available later at the same twelve-site price, just paid on top of this change rather than instead of it. Neutral for STORE-1, STORE-5 and HIST-2; leaves STORE-3's wrapper idiom as the only typed value in a file that had a second candidate for one.

**Recommendation: Typed OriginalCellOffset.** The two roads differ by nine functions in one private file, not by an order of magnitude: twelve mandatory sites against three, all inside `LogicalLineStore.swift`, with zero test edits either way. That is the whole price of the ideal, and the audit's "roughly seventeen sites" only reaches seventeen if the type is also pushed across the `RecordTextPosition` boundary, which the preparer already advises against and which I would explicitly rule out (it would pull in 21 lines of `TerminalSearch.swift` and put a wrapper inside a coordinate whose two-word storage a test pins). Two facts push past the raw count. First, the code holds nine hand-written `headTrimmedCells` conversions, and a plain rebase leaves every one of them free to feed a retained-relative Int into a key-taking parameter -- the exact move that produced this defect -- so option B fixes today's three writers and leaves the class intact. Second, the audit's own cheap fallback is worse than it looks: `precondition(headTrimmedCells == 0 || offsets.count > 1)` in `trimHeadRecord` guards a state that `makeRoom`'s eviction loop can legitimately reach (`LogicalLineStore.swift#makeRoom` calls `evictOneDisplayRow` on the sole open record when it cannot find contiguous room), so it would convert a latent misread into a live process trap, and the starter kit's failing test would trap instead of pass. Drop the precondition from the menu entirely. I also considered and rejected a third road -- delete the second base by having `trimHeadRecord` rewrite the record's table keys down to the trimmed base, so `headTrimmedCells` disappears from all nine sites. It is the simplest structure on paper, but the original base exists to keep coordinates stable across a trim (`recordCoordinateSurvivesHeadTrim`), and rebasing the arena would also add per-eviction work proportional to the identity table. If the owner wants the cheap road anyway, the honest version is option B without the precondition, and AGENTS.md asks that the typed shape be written into the plan as the deferred ideal.

### [HIST-5](#hist-5) -- Price the memory census by walking records, not by materializing every retained row

_Not priced yet; this is the question as the preparer stated it._

A human has to settle one question before the first line of production code:
does `memoryCensus.cellCount` (and `styledCellCount`, `hyperlinkCellCount`,
`contentIdentityCellCount`) keep counting painted cells -- trailing fill and
deferred spacer heads included, which is width-dependent -- or become a count
of stored cells, which is width-free and lowers
`coloredErasePaddingIsNotCompacted`'s expectation from 8+8 to 8+3? The finding
asserts both answers in different paragraphs. Choose stored cells and the
ideal record walk is buildable; choose painted cells and the honest
implementation is the finding's own streaming fallback, which removes the
whole-history peak without a new store read. Everything else in this kit --
the new `forEachContentIdentity`, the open-tail trap, the first failing test,
the safety net -- is ready to go the moment that is settled.

### [REDUCE-3](#reduce-3) -- Repair the focused pane's alerts in one pass instead of copying the rule into nine arms

_Not priced yet; this is the question as the preparer stated it._

A human must decide whether the `isAppActive` gate is acceptable. Today a
focus change clears the focused pane's alerts even while DanTerm is in the
background (an IPC `pane.focus` or `tab.select` from a script, for instance);
with the gate, that badge survives until the user foregrounds the app.
Everything else in this kit is ready, and the `closeTabRemoval` defect it
fixes is real and testable today. If the user says the gate is unacceptable,
the pass can drop `isAppActive` -- but then `.appBecameActive`'s copy no
longer falls out for free and the `.sessionBell` inactive path needs re-
checking, since a bell raised on the focused pane while inactive would be
cleared by the very next message.

## Settle these first

Groups whose members interact: one reverses another, one subsumes another, or
the order decides how much of the work survives. The `C` entries came out of the
round-1 synthesis; the `X` entries are cross-area collisions only the vetting
pass could see, because no single area auditor was looking at both halves.

### C1. [IPC-1](#ipc-1) + [IPC-4](#ipc-4) + [IPC-3](#ipc-3)

- [IPC-1](#ipc-1) -- Derive the IPC audit descriptor from the request's encoded params, not a third hand-written switch
- [IPC-4](#ipc-4) -- Return one traits value from a single exhaustive switch instead of six parallel per-method enumerations
- [IPC-3](#ipc-3) -- Give the todo state change one catalog case so three unreachable `preconditionFailure` arms disappear

**Issue.** All three rewrite the same `IpcRequestMethod`/`IpcRequest` projections. The audit-descriptor fix is specified in terms of `targetParameterKeys` and `params`, which the traits fix is simultaneously moving; and the todo collapse changes the case list both of them switch over. Doing them independently means each one is written against a case list and a key vocabulary the next one replaces, and the audit fix in particular could be built on the very duplicate key spellings the traits fix deletes.

**Resolution.** Settle the catalog shape first: collapse `todo.done`/`todo.open` into `todoSetDone` (small, self-contained), then land the single `traits` value plus one `targetParameterKeys`, then derive the audit descriptor from `params` filtered by those keys. The round-trip test `IpcRequestTests.everyCLIRequestRoundTripsThroughCatalog` is the fixed point that must keep passing through all three.

### C2. [MODEL-1](#model-1) + [CHROME-2](#chrome-2)

- [MODEL-1](#model-1) -- Replace PendingConfirmation's subject-plus-optional-payloads with one per-subject enum
- [CHROME-2](#chrome-2) -- Make the confirmation projection carry each button's answer instead of inferring it from button visibility

**Issue.** Both redesign the confirmation transaction end to end and disagree about where the kind lives. The enum fix keeps `ConfirmationSubject` (as a computed property) so confirm dispatch can match on it; the answer fix wants the panel to know no transaction kind at all and the reducer to switch on a `ConfirmationAnswer`. Doing the panel side first means writing an answer enum against a payload shape that is about to change; doing them separately means the reducer grows two dispatch vocabularies.

**Resolution.** Land the PendingConfirmation enum first, then define `ConfirmationAnswer` as a projection of that enum's cases and delete the `Msg.confirmConfirmation`/`chooseDeleteGroupConfirmation` pair in the same change, so there is one message (`.answerConfirmation(id:answer:)`) and one exhaustive switch.

### C3. [MODEL-5](#model-5) + [REDUCE-2](#reduce-2) + [REDUCE-5](#reduce-5)

- [MODEL-5](#model-5) -- Move per-pane search and notification-throttle state into PaneModel so pane teardown prunes them
- [REDUCE-2](#reduce-2) -- Let .startSearch open the pane's search state directly instead of round-tripping through the view
- [REDUCE-5](#reduce-5) -- Raise every pane alert through one function instead of duplicating the ritual in .sessionBell

**Issue.** The storage move relocates `model.searchState` and `model.lastNotificationTime` onto `PaneModel`. The other two write new code against exactly those two dictionaries -- a new `.startSearch` write site and a new `raiseAlert` helper holding the throttle call -- so doing them first means writing, reviewing, and testing code that the storage move immediately rewrites.

**Resolution.** Move the two side tables onto `PaneModel` first (it also shrinks `clearPaneSideTables` to the alert feed), then add the `.startSearch` direct write and the `raiseAlert` funnel against the new location.

### C4. [PERSIST-5](#persist-5) + [PERSIST-6](#persist-6) + [RUNTIME-6](#runtime-6) + [BUILD-1](#build-1)

- [PERSIST-5](#persist-5) -- Move the pure pane-tape stream policy into DanTermCore and leave only the socket write in Support
- [PERSIST-6](#persist-6) -- Publish the pane-tape record shape once in DanTermProtocol instead of writing keys on both sides
- [RUNTIME-6](#runtime-6) -- Move the pane-tape follow broker out of AppRuntime into its own owner
- [BUILD-1](#build-1) -- Declare each source target's purity profile once, and make the gate enumerate targets

**Issue.** Four findings move or re-own the same pane-tape code across three layers, and the fourth writes a gate that asserts the layer each file is allowed to occupy. Any order other than bottom-up means files are moved twice: the record builders cannot move into core while they still write untyped `[String: JSONValue]` literals that the client parses independently, and the purity declaration would be written against a layout the moves are about to change.

**Resolution.** Bottom-up: (1) define the typed `PaneTapeRecord` in DanTermProtocol and switch both producer and reader to it; (2) move the stream policy and record builders into DanTermCore and `writePaneTapeRecords` into app/; (3) extract the follow broker in app/; (4) declare the purity profiles last, so the gate records the settled layout rather than the transitional one.

### C5. [RUNTIME-1](#runtime-1) + [RUNTIME-3](#runtime-3)

- [RUNTIME-1](#runtime-1) -- Make the restore commit a Msg so `update()` is the only writer of `model`
- [RUNTIME-3](#runtime-3) -- Stop opening nested modal run loops from inside an open send frame

**Issue.** They overlap on the launch restore prompt and pull in opposite directions if ordered wrongly. The modal fix wants the restore prompt projected from a launch model slot with the choice arriving as a Msg; the restore fix wants `commitRestoreSession` reduced to staging plus one `send`. If the restore-as-Msg lands while `applicationDidFinishLaunching` still calls `alert.runModal()` after the IPC server is up, the new `.sessionRestored` Msg can be raced by an IPC-driven `update()` during the prompt -- exactly the discard the restore fix claims to remove.

**Resolution.** Project the restore prompt (and the config-error alert) as non-modal model-driven panels first, so nothing can re-enter `send()` mid-frame; then convert the restore commit itself into `.sessionRestored(model:)` and make `AppRuntime.model` `private(set)`.

### C6. [INTERACT-1](#interact-1) + [PARSE-6](#parse-6)

- [INTERACT-1](#interact-1) -- Refresh the search index through one history-mutation funnel instead of seven hand-placed calls
- [PARSE-6](#parse-6) -- Split the inspection layer and the state-synchronization encoder out of the Terminal struct

**Issue.** Both propose a different owner for the same search state. The funnel makes `history` private behind `withHistory` and keeps `search` on `Terminal`; the inspection lift moves `search` (with selection and links) into a `TerminalInspection` value whose only mutations are intent-level and take the projection as an argument. Building one and then the other means the search-refresh seam is designed twice.

**Resolution.** Decide the ownership question once, in favor of the inspection lift's direction, and make the history funnel its first slice: `withHistory` calls `inspection.resynchronize(with:)` on the way out. Land the funnel first (it removes a live process-trapping bug), but write it so the callback is the inspection API rather than a bare `search?.synchronizeIndex`.

### C7. [STORE-1](#store-1) + [STORE-3](#store-3) + [STORE-2](#store-2)

- [STORE-1](#store-1) -- Derive arena bytes-in-use from the ring cursors instead of maintaining it at twelve sites
- [STORE-3](#store-3) -- Give the 8-byte cell word one encode/decode type instead of eight hand-inlined shift sites
- [STORE-2](#store-2) -- Delete PackedRetainedRow's dead body and move the cell-word constants to the store that uses them

**Issue.** All three edit `LogicalLineStore` and its neighbours, and two of them touch the same append/trim/drop sites. Introducing `CellWord` first means rewriting lines that sit next to twelve `bytesInUse` mutations the other fix deletes, and both fixes want the cell-word constants -- which currently live inside the file the third fix deletes -- to be somewhere stable.

**Resolution.** Order: delete `bytesInUse` and its twelve mutation sites (it also fixes the live pad-byte over-charge), then move the cell-word constants onto `LogicalLineRecord.Header` and delete `PackedRetainedRow.swift` with its tests, then introduce `CellWord` on top of the now-single layout declaration.

### C8. [INTERACT-2](#interact-2) + [PANE-3](#pane-3)

- [INTERACT-2](#interact-2) -- Carry the normalized `TerminalViewportCell` into `TerminalPointerEvent` and decide link cancellation inside the policy
- [PANE-3](#pane-3) -- Record which button a press forwarded, replacing the two ad-hoc pairing booleans

**Issue.** Both rewrite `forwardPointerDown`/`forwardPointerUp` in `SwiftTerminalSessionView`, and they interact: the press-record fix exists partly because `forwardPointerDown` can drop a press when `normalizedCell` returns nil, while the pointer-event fix removes that failure mode by making the cell (including `isInsideGrid`) part of every event. Landing the booleans fix first bakes in a guard that the other fix deletes.

**Resolution.** Change `TerminalPointerEvent` to carry the `TerminalViewportCell` first and delete the out-of-band `cancelLinkInteraction` path; then replace `rightButtonForwarded` and `controlClickIsActive` with the single `forwardedButton` record, which by then has no nil-cell early return to reason about.

### C9. [PERSIST-5](#persist-5) + [RUNTIME-6](#runtime-6)

- [PERSIST-5](#persist-5) -- Move the pure pane-tape stream policy into DanTermCore and leave only the socket write in Support
- [RUNTIME-6](#runtime-6) -- Move the pane-tape follow broker out of AppRuntime into its own owner

**Issue.** The broker extraction defines its entry points against where the policy currently lives (DanTermSupport). If the broker is extracted first, its init signature and session-lookup closure are written against Support-layer types that the layer move relocates, so the new type is edited immediately after it is created.

**Resolution.** Move the policy into core first, then extract the broker against the core-layer policy types; see the four-way pane-tape ordering above for the full sequence.

### C10. [PERSIST-2](#persist-2) + [PERSIST-1](#persist-1)

- [PERSIST-2](#persist-2) -- Give the recovery directory one owner: a RecoveryPaths value threaded from launch
- [PERSIST-1](#persist-1) -- Decide crash recovery from the lock file's existence, not from decoding it

**Issue.** Both change the session-lock API in `RecoveryStore`. The existence fix replaces `readSessionLockFile` with `hasSessionLock(...)` and makes the writer throw; the paths fix changes what every one of those functions takes. Doing the existence fix first means its new signatures are rewritten by the paths fix, and doing them independently keeps the demonstrated split-directory bug (lock and checkpoints resolving differently) alive under a new API.

**Resolution.** Introduce `RecoveryPaths` first and thread it from launch through every read/write/delete, then reshape the lock decision to `hasSessionLock(_:)` plus a throwing writer on top of it -- at which point a test can finally exercise write-checkpoints, write-lock, relaunch, merge in one redirected directory.

### X1. [INTERACT-1](#interact-1) + [FIND-1](#find-1) + [PARSE-6](#parse-6)

- [INTERACT-1](#interact-1) -- Refresh the search index through one history-mutation funnel instead of seven hand-placed calls
- [FIND-1](#find-1) -- Narrow the closed-history index on needle append instead of rebuilding it per keystroke
- [PARSE-6](#parse-6) -- Split the inspection layer and the state-synchronization encoder out of the Terminal struct

**Issue.** Three findings across three areas propose a different owner for the same search state. INTERACT-1 makes history private behind a `withHistory` funnel that calls `synchronizeSearchIndexPrefix`; FIND-1 replaces that whole-index rebuild with an incremental narrowing driven by needle append; PARSE-6 moves `search` off Terminal entirely into a TerminalInspection value. Whoever goes second writes against a seam the third one deletes.

**Resolution.** Land INTERACT-1 first (it removes a live process-trapping bug) but write the funnel callback as an inspection-shaped API, not a bare `search?.synchronizeIndex` call. Then FIND-1 changes what that callback does, not where it is called from. PARSE-6 last, in wave 5, moving an already-single call site.

### X2. [FEED-1](#feed-1) + [ROW-2](#row-2) + [ROW-4](#row-4) + [FEED-2](#feed-2)

- [FEED-1](#feed-1) -- Represent the viewport as a rotating row ring so a scroll advances a head index instead of moving every row
- [ROW-2](#row-2) -- Move multi-scalar spills out of GridCell so a live cell is trivially copyable and 16 bytes
- [ROW-4](#row-4) -- Write each printed cell once: clearCellAndPair's store at the target column is immediately overwritten
- [FEED-2](#feed-2) -- Reach a row's cells once per run, not once per cell, on the bulk ASCII write and scan loops

**Issue.** The feed and row-layout areas both rewrite how a printed cell reaches memory, and neither auditor saw the other. FEED-1 makes the viewport a rotating ring of rows; ROW-2 changes what a cell is (moving spills out of GridCell); ROW-4 and FEED-2 change how a run of cells is written. Doing ROW-2 first means the ring is built against a cell type that is itself in motion; doing FEED-1 first means ROW-2's measurement arm no longer exists.

**Resolution.** FEED-2 and ROW-4 first (both small, both confirmed, neither changes a type). FEED-1 next, since it only moves rows, not cells. ROW-2 last, in wave 5 -- it was downgraded to 3x3 large and is the only one of the four whose payoff is speculative.

### X3. [PERSIST-6](#persist-6) + [WIRE-2](#wire-2) + [WIRE-3](#wire-3) + [PERSIST-5](#persist-5) + [RUNTIME-6](#runtime-6) + [BUILD-1](#build-1) + [PERSIST-4](#persist-4)

- [PERSIST-6](#persist-6) -- Publish the pane-tape record shape once in DanTermProtocol instead of writing keys on both sides
- [WIRE-2](#wire-2) -- Carry a tape record as its typed event, not as a JSONValue decoded from its own encoding
- [WIRE-3](#wire-3) -- Encode a delivered tape batch as one notification off the main actor, not one per record
- [PERSIST-5](#persist-5) -- Move the pure pane-tape stream policy into DanTermCore and leave only the socket write in Support
- [RUNTIME-6](#runtime-6) -- Move the pane-tape follow broker out of AppRuntime into its own owner
- [BUILD-1](#build-1) -- Declare each source target's purity profile once, and make the gate enumerate targets
- [PERSIST-4](#persist-4) -- Confine the IPC connection's descriptor to its write queue so a queued write cannot land on a reused fd

**Issue.** Four areas (PERSIST, WIRE, RUNTIME, BUILD) move or re-own the same pane-tape code across three layers, and a fifth writes a gate asserting which layer each file may occupy. Separately, PERSIST-4 and WIRE-3 both rewrite `IpcConnection.writeLine` -- one confining the descriptor to the write queue, the other moving the encode off the main actor -- and the two area verifiers each saw only their own half.

**Resolution.** Strictly bottom-up: PERSIST-6 (typed record in DanTermProtocol) and PERSIST-4 (fd confinement) first; then WIRE-2/WIRE-3/WIRE-6 against the typed record and the confined descriptor; then PERSIST-5 (policy into core); then RUNTIME-6 (broker extraction against core types); BUILD-1 last, recording the settled layout.

### X4. [MODEL-3](#model-3) + [RECON-1](#recon-1) + [RUNTIME-5](#runtime-5) + [LOOKUP-4](#lookup-4) + [PANE-1](#pane-1)

- [MODEL-3](#model-3) -- Collapse ContainerShape to layout plus zoomedLeaf; derive the structural fingerprint
- [RECON-1](#recon-1) -- Make container visibility a diffed field of ContainerShape instead of an unconditional per-tab op
