##### PARSE-6. Split the inspection layer and the state-synchronization encoder out of the Terminal struct

`structural` &middot; impact 2, confidence 3 &middot; effort large &middot; wave 5 &middot; rewritten

**Files.** `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/Terminal.swift#Terminal`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/Terminal.swift#invalidateInspection`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/Terminal.swift#clearInspection`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/Terminal.swift#refreshHasContentInspectionState`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/Terminal.swift#encodeStateSynchronization`

**Problem.** `Terminal` is a single 7.6k-line struct carrying roughly sixty stored properties and doing at least five separable jobs: escape dispatch and grid mutation, width/height reflow, scrollback and eviction, user inspection (selection, search, hovered and armed links, viewport anchoring, row-numbering epochs), and the state-synchronization byte encoder. Every private method can write every field, so cross-job invariants -- "a grid mutation that overwrites content retires the link state anchored there", "a history mutation resynchronizes the search index" -- are upheld by remembering to call a function, and the compiler cannot help.

**Evidence.** The inspection fields (`selection`, `selectionRequiresNonemptyReflowResult`, `search`, `hoveredLinkState`, `armedLinkState`, `hoveredLinkRevisionCounter`, `hasContentInspectionState`, `viewportState`, `rowNumberingEpoch`, `evictedRowCount`) are plain private vars sitting alongside `screen`, `history`, `modes` and `styleTable`. Their coherence is maintained by property observers (`didSet { refreshHasContentInspectionState() }` on three of them) and by grid code remembering to call one of four differently scoped entry points -- `invalidateInspection(inViewportRows:)`, `invalidateInspectionState(inViewportRows:)`, `invalidateInspection(inScrollbackRow:)`, `synchronizeSearchIndexPrefix()` -- which a new mutation path must pick correctly from. Separately, `encodeStateSynchronization` and its helpers (`appendControlState`, `appendSavedCursor`, `appendModes`, `appendSemanticState`, `appendGraphemeSynchronization`, `boundedHistoryStart`, `alignedHistoryStart`) are roughly 350 lines that only read state and emit bytes.

**Ideal fix.** Two extractions, independently landable. First, lift the inspection fields into a `TerminalInspection` value that owns them and exposes only intent-level mutations (`invalidate(absoluteRows:)`, `clear()`, `resynchronize(with:)`), with the projection passed in as an argument; `Terminal` then holds one `inspection` field and grid code can reach that state only through the API. Second, move the state-synchronization encoder into its own type in its own file, constructed from a read-only view of the terminal. Both shrink `Terminal` to parser plus grid plus reflow and give each extracted job a testable surface of its own.

**By construction.** After the inspection lift, grid and parser code cannot assign to `selection`, `search` or the link slots at all; the only way to affect them is the invalidation API, so "a new mutation path that writes inspection state directly and skips the damage bookkeeping" stops being expressible.

**Cheaper fallback.** If the inspection lift proves too entangled with reflow's anchor capture and restatement, do the state-synchronization encoder alone -- it is pure read-and-emit -- and leave inspection in place with a written note that the lift is the remaining half.

**Verification.** No behavior may change, so the proof is the existing `TerminalCoreTests` suites (selection, search, hyperlink interaction, stale-wrap-claim, state-synchronization round trips) passing unchanged, plus a state-synchronization round-trip test that feeds an encoded snapshot into a fresh terminal and asserts equality of projected text, cursor, modes and styles.

**Risk.** The inspection lift touches reflow's anchor capture and restatement, the most delicate code in the file; the round-trip and selection-across-resize tests keep it honest, and the encoder extraction can ship first to de-risk the sequencing.

**Vetted.** Confirmed the size (7,602 lines, ~106 var declarations) and that the inspection fields and their three `didSet { refreshHasContentInspectionState() }` observers sit inline with `screen`/`history`/`modes`, and that the four differently scoped invalidation entry points exist and are called from ~15 grid sites. But two of the ten fields the finding wants to lift are not inspection state: `evictedRowCount` is a history coordinate (`absoluteViewportTopRow` is `evictedRowCount + scrollProjection.topRow`, and its own doc comment explains its relationship to `historyEvictionsObserved` and hard reset), and `rowNumberingEpoch` is grid row numbering that `hardReset`/`switchAlternateScreen` restart. Moving either into a `TerminalInspection` value would be wrong. Also, the block comment above the fields documents `hasContentInspectionState` as a deliberate hot-path cache read once per printed character so the guard is "one Bool load instead of three optional loads" -- the lift must preserve that, which the finding does not say. The encoder half is clean and independently landable; the inspection half is speculative (no cited bug) and the riskiest code in the file.

**Correction.** Split this into two findings with different scores. (a) Extract the state-synchronization encoder (`encodeStateSynchronization`, `appendControlState`, `appendSavedCursor`, `appendModes`, `appendSemanticState`, `appendGraphemeSynchronization`, `boundedHistoryStart`, `alignedHistoryStart`) into its own type in its own file, constructed from a read-only view: pure read-and-emit, ~350 lines, effort medium, impact 3. (b) The inspection lift is impact 2 / confidence 2 and should be scoped to the six fields that really are inspection state -- `selection`, `selectionRequiresNonemptyReflowResult`, `search`, `hoveredLinkState`, `armedLinkState`, `hoveredLinkRevisionCounter`, plus the derived `hasContentInspectionState` -- and must keep `hasContentInspectionState` as a one-Bool-load guard on the per-printed-character path, which its own comment says is why it exists. `evictedRowCount` and `rowNumberingEpoch` stay on `Terminal`: they are history/grid coordinates, not inspection state.

**Sharper ideal.** Land the encoder extraction alone. It carries essentially all of the confirmed value at a fraction of the risk, and it is the half the finding's own cheaper fallback already picks.

**Do after.** [PARSE-2](#parse-2), [PARSE-3](#parse-3)

**Conflicts with.** [PARSE-2](#parse-2), [PARSE-3](#parse-3), [FEED-3](#feed-3)

#### Area: Scrollback and row storage (`STORE`)

_Scope: Scrollback and row storage (LogicalLineStore, LogicalLineRecord, PackedRetainedRow, TerminalMemoryCensus, Instruments, TerminalGeometry)_

**The auditor's read on the area.** The doc-31 arena store is unusually disciplined: the two grand totals are already derived off the block ring, the side-table charge has a recount oracle asserted in `census`, and the fold has one shared shape function feeding all three read walks. The residue is concentrated in three places -- the one remaining hand-maintained byte total (`bytesInUse`), the previous representation (`PackedRetainedRow`) that survives only as a constant namespace, and a handful of hand-copied arithmetic idioms (cell-word decode, block-to-record-range). I did not audit `Terminal.swift`'s side of the seam (anchors, projections, admission triggers) or the test files beyond checking which oracles exist; `TerminalGeometry.swift` is plain read-only value types and yielded nothing.

##### STORE-1. Derive arena bytes-in-use from the ring cursors instead of maintaining it at twelve sites

`structural` &middot; impact 4, confidence 5 &middot; effort medium &middot; wave 1 &middot; rewritten

**Files.** `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#dropTailRecord`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#wrapWriteCursorAtSeam`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#chargedBytes`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#census`

**Problem.** `bytesInUse` is the term that directly bounds `31/I2`, and it is the one maintained total in this file with no owner and no oracle. Twelve mutation sites add or subtract it by hand (`openRecordIfNeeded`, `appendCells`, `appendBlankCells`, `closeOpenRecord`, `forceSplitOpenRecord`, `reopenClosedTail`, `cutTail`, `trimHeadRecord`, `dropHeadRecord`, `dropTailRecord`, `wrapWriteCursorAtSeam`, `resetToEmptyArena`), while the side-table charge next to it gets `recountedChargedBytes` plus an `assert` in `census`, and the row and content totals get `independentDisplayRowRecount` / `independentContentUnitRecount`. One of the twelve is already wrong: tail truncation across a chunk-boundary pad leaves the pad's bytes charged, so history over-charges and evicts earlier than the budget requires.

**Evidence.** The in-use region is by construction the ring span `[head, writeCursor)`, and every site moves the cursor and the counter by the same amount: `openRecordIfNeeded` does `writeCursor += Header.byteCount; bytesInUse += Header.byteCount`; `closeOpenRecord` does `bytesInUse += record.byteLength - headerAndCells(record.cellCount)` with `writeCursor = recordOffset(in: offset) + record.byteLength`; `dropHeadRecord` subtracts exactly the ring distance `nextOffset > oldOffset ? nextOffset - oldOffset : (arenaCapacity - oldOffset) + nextOffset` and sets `head = nextOffset`; `wrapWriteCursorAtSeam` charges a pad at `bytesInUse += pad.byteLength` and sets `writeCursor = boundary`. The exception is `dropTailRecord`, which does `bytesInUse -= record.byteLength; writeCursor = recordOffset(in: offset)` -- when the dropped record is the first one after a chunk-boundary pad, the cursor moves back past the pad but the pad's bytes are never subtracted. `writeCursorPrecedesHead` already needs the empty/full disambiguation (`bytesInUse > 0 && writeCursor <= head`) that a derived form would take from `offsets.count`.

**Ideal fix.** Delete the stored `bytesInUse` field and all twelve of its mutations, and make it computed: `offsets.count == 0 ? 0 : (writeCursor > head ? writeCursor - head : arenaCapacity - head + writeCursor)`. `writeCursorPrecedesHead` becomes `offsets.count > 0 && writeCursor <= head`. Nothing else changes -- `head` and `writeCursor` are already moved correctly at every site, pads included.

**By construction.** A mutation that moves arena bytes without moving their charge stops being expressible: there is no charge to move. The pad-leak class -- any byte the ring cursor skips over but the counter still holds -- becomes unrepresentable, because the counter is the cursor distance.

**Cheaper fallback.** Keep the field, subtract the pad in `dropTailRecord` by comparing the dropped record's offset against the predecessor record's end, and add an `independentArenaBytesInUse` recount asserted in `census` beside the existing side-table assert. This leaves twelve maintenance sites and pins only the one bug already found.

**Verification.** Behavioral test at a budget small enough that a chunk boundary falls a few display rows from the tail: admit rows until `wrapWriteCursorAtSeam` has written a pad, then `truncateTail(displayRows:)` past the pad, and assert `store.census.arenaBytesInUse` matches the same store rebuilt by admitting only the surviving rows -- or, observably, that admitting N further rows after the truncation retains the same record count as admitting N rows into a fresh store at the same content. Today the truncated store retains fewer records.

**Risk.** The derived form is read on the write path (`chargedBytes`, once per admission and once per eviction step); it is two comparisons and a subtraction, cheaper than the load it replaces. The only care needed is that `resetToEmptyArena` keeps setting `head == writeCursor == 0` so the empty case stays unambiguous.

**Vetted.** Read every `bytesInUse` site in `LogicalLineStore.swift` (13 statements across the 12 named functions) and confirmed each moves `writeCursor` by the same amount it charges: `openRecordIfNeeded`, `appendCells`, `appendBlankCells`, `closeOpenRecord`, `forceSplitOpenRecord`, `reopenClosedTail`, `cutTail`, `trimHeadRecord`, `dropHeadRecord`, `dropTailRecord`, `wrapWriteCursorAtSeam` (twice), `resetToEmptyArena`. `head` is kept equal to `offsets[0]`'s offset by every mutator and the arena is fully covered by pads at every seam, so the ring distance `[head, writeCursor)` is exactly the charged arena span and the derived form is sound. The pad leak is real but the finding names the wrong trigger: dropping the record *after* a pad sets `writeCursor` to that record's offset, which is the pad's end, so nothing leaks there. The leak fires when the cursor rewinds to *before* a pad -- `dropTailRecord` on the last record preceding the pad, and `cutTail` inside a forced-split record that `reopenTailRecordForTruncation` reopened. `reopenTailRecord`'s own comment names this exact hazard ("Rewinding the write cursor to before that pad would make the next wrap re-pad and double-charge, so resuming a print never reopens one") and then routes truncation through the path that does rewind, so the double-charge the comment forbids on the print path is reachable on the resize/reflow path (`truncateTail` is called from two sites in `Terminal.swift`). Commit `1c6bcf1f` ("derive the grand totals instead of storing them") already took this exact step for the row and content totals, so the change continues an accepted direction rather than opening one.

**Correction.** The over-charge does not happen when the dropped record is the first one after a chunk-boundary pad -- there `writeCursor` lands on the pad's end and the pad is still inside the in-use span, correctly charged. It happens when the write cursor rewinds to *before* a pad: `dropTailRecord` on the record that precedes the pad subtracts only that record's `byteLength` while the span loses the record plus the whole pad, and `cutTail` inside a forced-split record reopened by `reopenTailRecordForTruncation` rewinds the cursor past the pad and subtracts only the cut cells. Both are reachable from `truncateTail(displayRows:)`, which resize and reflow call to pull rows back into the live grid. The leaked bytes are never recovered short of `resetToEmptyArena`, and the next wrap writes and charges a fresh pad over the same region, so repeated resizes make history charge more than it holds and evict earlier than the budget requires.

**Conflicts with.** [STORE-3](#store-3), [STORE-2](#store-2)

<details>
<summary><b>Starter kit</b> -- current shape, 16 change sites, the tests, and the first failing test</summary>

**Current shape.** `Terminal.LogicalLineStore` in `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift` holds three private ring fields side by side: `private var head = 0` (byte offset of the oldest retained record's header), `private var writeCursor = 0` (byte offset where the next bytes go, wrapping to 0 at the physical end) and `private var bytesInUse = 0`. `bytesInUse` is read by exactly three things -- `var chargedBytes: Int { bytesInUse + indexChargeBytes + openScratchBytes + sideTables.chargedBytes }`, `var census: Census` (which passes it as `arenaBytesInUse:`), and `private var writeCursorPrecedesHead: Bool { bytesInUse > 0 && writeCursor <= head }` -- and it is written at 13 statements across 12 mutating functions. Nothing has moved since the finding was written: the newest commit on this file is `1c6bcf1f` ("derive the grand totals instead of storing them"), which is the same move applied to `grandDisplayRowTotal` and `grandContentUnitTotal`, and its rationale comment on `grandDisplayRowTotal` is the model for this one. `arenaCapacity`, `head` and `writeCursor` are all plain `Int` byte offsets over one linear ring `[0, arenaCapacity)`, and every seam in the arena is covered by a pad record (`LogicalLineRecord(cellCount:isPad:)`) because `wrapWriteCursorAtSeam` only skips the pad when the remainder is exactly zero.

**Change sites.**

- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#LogicalLineStore` -- Delete `private var bytesInUse = 0` and add a computed `private var bytesInUse: Int` (or name it `arenaBytesInUse`) reading `offsets.count == 0 ? 0 : (writeCursor > head ? writeCursor - head : arenaCapacity - head + writeCursor)`. Give it a `///` comment on the same pattern as `grandDisplayRowTotal`'s: the in-use region *is* the ring span, so a byte the cursor skips can no longer stay charged.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#openRecordIfNeeded` -- Delete `bytesInUse += LogicalLineRecord.Header.byteCount` (the `writeCursor += Header.byteCount` above it stays).
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#appendCells` -- Delete `bytesInUse += cells.count * LogicalLineRecord.cellBytes`.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#appendBlankCells` -- Delete `bytesInUse += count * LogicalLineRecord.cellBytes`.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#closeOpenRecord` -- Delete `bytesInUse += record.byteLength - LogicalLineRecord.headerAndCells(record.cellCount)` (the tables the close flushes are already covered by the `writeCursor = recordOffset(in: offset) + record.byteLength` on the next line).
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#forceSplitOpenRecord` -- Delete the identical `bytesInUse +=` statement.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#reopenClosedTail` -- Delete `bytesInUse -= closedLength - record.byteLength`; `let closedLength = record.byteLength` then becomes unused and must go too.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#trimHeadRecord` -- Delete `bytesInUse -= cut * LogicalLineRecord.cellBytes`; `head = newOffset` above it already states the same fact.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#dropHeadRecord` -- Delete the three-line `bytesInUse -= nextOffset > oldOffset ? ... : (arenaCapacity - oldOffset) + nextOffset`, plus the now-dead `let oldOffset`. The comment above it ("Reading the span off the index rather than re-deriving...") should be rewritten or dropped: it explains an arithmetic that is disappearing.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#dropTailRecord` -- Delete `bytesInUse -= record.byteLength`. This is one of the two leak sites: `writeCursor = recordOffset(in: offset)` may rewind past a pad the subtraction never accounts for.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#cutTail` -- Delete `bytesInUse -= (oldCellCount - newCellCount) * LogicalLineRecord.cellBytes`. Second leak site: reached through `reopenTailRecordForTruncation` on a forced-split tail, whose pad the rewind skips.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#wrapWriteCursorAtSeam` -- Two deletions: `bytesInUse -= LogicalLineRecord.Header.byteCount` in the empty-open-record discard branch, and `bytesInUse += pad.byteLength` after the pad is written. The comment "Charged at the pad's own length, which is what the head subtracts when it skips it, so the two can never drift" goes with it -- under the derived form there is nothing to drift.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#resetToEmptyArena` -- Delete `bytesInUse = 0`. `head = 0` and `writeCursor = 0` must stay, and the doc for the derived property should say why: they are what keeps the empty case unambiguous.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#writeCursorPrecedesHead` -- Becomes `offsets.count > 0 && writeCursor <= head`. Do this rather than leaving it reading the derived property: the derived property is defined in terms of this same disambiguation, so keeping the old spelling would be circular.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#chargedBytes` -- No text change, but it now reads a computed property on the write path. Its doc comment says "every term is either capacity arithmetic or a total its owner maintains" -- update it to say the arena term is now the ring span itself.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#census` -- `arenaBytesInUse: bytesInUse` keeps compiling unchanged. Consider whether the `assert` that guards the side-table charge deserves a sibling note that the arena term no longer needs one.

**Tests that must keep passing.** These are the safety net.

- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- chargedBytesStayUnderTheBudget -- the `31/I2` bound on both content and blank histories, plus `arenaBytesInUse > 0` before `removeAll` and `== 0` after
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- censusSeparatesCapacityFromBytesInUse -- 0 on a fresh store, >0 and <capacity after one admission, and chargedBytes decomposing into the three terms
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- widthChangeIsANoOpOnRetainedStorage -- `arenaBytesInUse` unchanged across five width changes
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- closeAndReopenTheTailRecord -- `arenaBytesInUse` identical before close, after close and after reopen; this is the tightest pin on the close/reopen pair of mutations being deleted
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- maintainedChargeAgreesWithARecount -- charge equals the census recount after admission, three width changes, head eviction, tail truncation, forced split, reopen and clear
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- cyclingTheRingPreservesTheRetainedSuffix -- 900 lines through several full wraps with interleaved evictions, asserting chargedBytes <= capacity throughout
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- openTailForcedSplitsAtThePhysicalEnd -- the pad-and-split seam, chargedBytes bounded at every step
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- emptyOpenRecordAtTheSeamNeedsNoSplit -- the empty-open-record branch of `wrapWriteCursorAtSeam`, whose `bytesInUse -=` is being deleted
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- ringCyclesAcrossChunkSeamsAndKeepsItsRetainedSuffix -- chunk-boundary pads specifically
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- sideTableChargeDecidesRetentionDepth -- an exact retention depth, so a charge that shifts by even one pad changes the answer
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalScrollbackBudgetTests.swift -- historyChargesOneHeaderPerRecord (the fixture loop asserting `arenaBytesInUse == (expected + 7) & ~7`) -- exact byte equality per record shape
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalScrollbackBudgetTests.swift -- eraseDisplayThreeResetsBudgetState -- >0 then ==0 across ED 3
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalRegionScrollbackTests.swift -- regionPushesObeyScrollbackBudget -- `arenaBytesInUse == lineCost`, `== lineCost * 2`, and unchanged after the evicting push

**Tests that will need updating.** Expect these; they assert the thing being changed.

- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- none identified -- every existing assertion is on `census.arenaBytesInUse` or `chargedBytes`, both of which keep their spelling and their meaning; no test names `bytesInUse` or reaches into `head`/`writeCursor`
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLinePathologicalProbe.swift -- pathologicalSingleLine and its siblings -- only print `retainedArenaBytesInUse` and assert it is <= capacity, and the suite is env-gated; no edit expected, but the printed numbers will change wherever a leak was being reported

**Write this test first.** Suite `Logical-line record arena` (`lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift`), new test "A tail truncation across the ring's wrap seam gives its bytes back". Scenario: build a control store and a subject store at the same small budget (1 << 16) and width, and feed both the same long run of uniform hard-ended rows -- enough to wrap the ring several times, which `cyclingTheRingPreservesTheRetainedSuffix` shows 900 lines at budget 1 << 15 does comfortably. The subject store reaches that same final content through cycles of `truncateTail(displayRows: 1)` followed by two admissions, so the write cursor repeatedly rewinds across the pad `wrapWriteCursorAtSeam` wrote at a seam and then advances past it again. Assertion: `subject.grandDisplayRowTotal == control.grandDisplayRowTotal` and `foldedScalars(subject) == foldedScalars(control)`. Why it fails today: each rewind past a pad leaves the pad's bytes charged (`dropTailRecord` subtracts only `record.byteLength`, `cutTail` only the cut cells), the next wrap writes and charges a fresh pad over the same region, so the subject's `chargedBytes` climbs above the control's for identical content and `evictToBudget` drops rows the control keeps -- the subject retains strictly fewer display rows. Note for the implementer: the leak is only recovered by `resetToEmptyArena`, so keep the cycle count high enough to accumulate several pads but the content well short of driving the subject to zero records, and pin the exact expected depth from the control store rather than from a literal. If a tighter, single-shot pin is wanted alongside it, the byte-level form is `#expect(subject.census.arenaBytesInUse == control.census.arenaBytesInUse)` for two stores that hold the same records at the same head offset -- but the row-depth form is the one that states the user-visible harm, and it is the one to write first.

**Blockers and surprises.** Three things worth knowing before starting. First, `maintainedChargeAgreesWithARecount` is weaker than its name suggests: `census.chargedBytes` is built from the same stored `bytesInUse` that `chargedBytes` reads, so that test cannot catch an arena-term drift at all -- it only guards the side-table term, which has its own `recountedChargedBytes` oracle. Do not treat it as the safety net for this change. Second, `reopenTailRecord` carries a comment that names this exact hazard -- "Rewinding the write cursor to before that pad would make the next wrap re-pad and double-charge, so resuming a print never reopens one. Truncation, which is a rewind by construction, goes through `reopenTailRecordForTruncation` instead" -- and `reopenTailRecordForTruncation` then performs the rewind the comment forbids. That comment needs rewriting as part of the change, because under the derived form the rewind is safe and the guard on `reopenTailRecord` is about the forced-split bit, not about charge. Third, the derived form must not be applied before checking the two empty/full edges by hand: `writeCursor == head` with `offsets.count > 0` is a full ring and must yield `arenaCapacity` (the `writeCursor > head` branch is false, so `arenaCapacity - head + writeCursor` gives exactly that), and `resetToEmptyArena` must keep setting both cursors to 0. Everything else is clean: `bytesInUse` appears nowhere outside this file, `Terminal.memoryCensus` reads `arena.arenaBytesInUse` off the `Census` value whose shape does not change, `TerminalMemoryCensus` (public, in `lib/`) is untouched, and equality (`recordsEqual`) never reads the field. On performance, the derived form is two comparisons and a subtraction on a path that read one field, and `1c6bcf1f` already set the precedent for exactly this trade on the same file.

**Readiness: ready.** An agent can start on this from the above.

<a id="store-2"></a>

##### STORE-2. Delete PackedRetainedRow's dead body and move the cell-word constants to the store that uses them

`simplification` &middot; impact 3, confidence 5 &middot; effort medium &middot; wave 2 &middot; confirmed

**Files.** `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/PackedRetainedRow.swift#PackedRetainedRow`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineRecord.swift#LogicalLineRecord`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#appendCells`

**Problem.** `PackedRetainedRow` is the pre-doc-31 per-display-row representation. Nothing in production constructs, stores, or reads one any more -- the logical-line arena replaced it. What survives is a 643-line type whose only live export is the `Header` enum's cell-word constants, plus a ~420-line test file exercising an encoding the engine no longer produces. A reader working on row storage faces two full layout contracts, one of which is a fiction, and the constants the real store depends on are declared inside the fiction.

**Evidence.** `git grep -l PackedRetainedRow -- '*.swift'` returns seven files. In `Terminal.swift` and `LogicalLineRecord.swift` every hit is a comment. In `LogicalLineStore.swift` every hit is `PackedRetainedRow.Header.<constant>` (`cellKindShift`, `cellKindMask`, `cellScalarMask`, `cellSpillBit`, `cellStyleShift`, `cellBytes`, `hyperlinkEntryBytes`, `identityRunEntryBytes`, `identityCellBytes`). The type's own members -- `pack(_:)`, `unpacked()`, `forEachCell`, `forEachContentCell`, `forEachKind`, `cell(at:)`, `storedCellCount`, `spills`, `storage` -- appear nowhere outside `PackedRetainedRow.swift` and `TerminalPackedRetainedRowTests.swift`. `Header` also mixes two layouts: `byteCount = 7`, `softWrapBit`, `promptShift`, `identityPerCellBit` describe the dead blob header, while `cellScalarMask`/`cellKindShift`/`cellStyleShift`/`cellSpillBit` describe the 8-byte cell word the arena still writes.

**Ideal fix.** Lift the eight-byte cell word into its own small type owned beside `LogicalLineRecord` (see the next finding), move `cellBytes`/`hyperlinkEntryBytes`/`identityRunEntryBytes`/`identityCellBytes` onto `LogicalLineRecord.Header` where the store's aliases already point, then delete `PackedRetainedRow.swift` and `TerminalPackedRetainedRowTests.swift` outright. Rewrite the few doc comments that cite `PackedRetainedRow.pack`'s trimming rule to state the rule directly.

**By construction.** There stops being a second, stale answer to "how is a retained row laid out": the arena record becomes the only stored form in the tree, so neither a reader nor a future change can pick the wrong one, and a layout constant can no longer be edited in a file whose tests do not cover the code that uses it.

**Cheaper fallback.** Keep the file but strip it to the cell-word constants and rename it for what it is. That removes the misleading second contract without the test-file churn, but leaves a namespace named after a representation that no longer exists.

**Verification.** `just test` after deletion -- the retained read-path suites (`TerminalRetainedRowReadPathTests`, `TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests`) already assert the arena's decode behavior per cell, so their staying green with `PackedRetainedRow` gone is the proof that nothing observable depended on it.

**Risk.** Deleting `TerminalPackedRetainedRowTests` removes coverage of the canonical-trim and identity-run rules as `pack` stated them; before deleting, confirm each rule the store still relies on (the strict-step-of-one run shape, the trailing-blank trim asymmetry) is asserted somewhere in the arena suites, and add it there if not.

**Vetted.** `grep -rn PackedRetainedRow lib app --include='*.swift'` confirms the claim exactly: outside its own 643-line file the only non-comment references are `PackedRetainedRow.Header.<constant>` in `LogicalLineStore.swift` and the four aliases on `LogicalLineRecord.Header` (`cellBytes`, `hyperlinkEntryBytes`, `identityRunEntryBytes`, `identityCellBytes`), plus `TerminalPackedRetainedRowTests.swift` (419 lines, 11 `@Test`s). `pack`, `unpacked`, `cell(at:)`, `forEachCell`, `forEachContentCell`, `forEachKind`, `storedCellCount`, `spills`, `storage` have no production caller. The file header still asserts the type is what history stores, which `LogicalLineRecord.swift` contradicts. The probe island that the plan `plans/impl/2026-08-17-1110-retire-logical-line-probe-island.md` says still compiled against `PackedRetainedRow` is already gone from the main tree, so nothing outside the tests holds it up. Risk section is the right one: the arena's canonical-trim and strict-step-of-one identity-run rules are stated in `LogicalLineStore` comments as "matching `PackedRetainedRow.pack`", so those cases need retargeting rather than deleting.

**Sharper ideal.** Moving the constants onto `LogicalLineRecord.Header` (where the aliases already point) is the right landing site and is cheaper than inventing a separate namespace; STORE-3's `CellWord` should then be built on top of that single declaration, not beside it.

**Do after.** [STORE-1](#store-1)

**Conflicts with.** [ROW-1](#row-1) (pruned)

**Absorbs.** [ROW-1](#row-1) was pruned in favour of this finding; the [Pruned](#pruned) entry says which of its points to carry over.

<a id="store-3"></a>

##### STORE-3. Give the 8-byte cell word one encode/decode type instead of eight hand-inlined shift sites

`structural` &middot; impact 3, confidence 5 &middot; effort small &middot; wave 3 &middot; confirmed

**Files.** `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#withPaintedCells`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#forEachClosedRecordCell`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#appendCells`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#forEachKind`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#forEachStyleId`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#cellKind`

**Problem.** The cell word's field extraction is written out by hand at eight places in `LogicalLineStore`, each repeating the same shift-and-mask triple. The kind decode alone appears five times verbatim. A change to the word layout -- widening the scalar field, moving the style, adding a flag -- must be found and applied at all eight, and a site that gets one shift wrong decodes plausible-looking garbage rather than failing to compile.

**Evidence.** `TerminalCellKind(packedCode: UInt8((word >> PackedRetainedRow.Header.cellKindShift) & PackedRetainedRow.Header.cellKindMask))` is written out in `forEachClosedRecordCell`, `withPaintedCells`, `forEachKind`, `cell(recordIndex:recordOffset:record:cellOffset:)`, and `cellKind(recordAt:cell:)`. `Terminal.StyleId(truncatingIfNeeded: word >> PackedRetainedRow.Header.cellStyleShift)` appears in `withPaintedCells` twice (once for the spacer word), in `forEachStyleId`, and in `cell(...)`. `let field = UInt32(word & PackedRetainedRow.Header.cellScalarMask)` followed by a `word & cellSpillBit` test appears in `forEachClosedRecordCell`, `withPaintedCells`, and `cell(...)`. The write side is spelled once in `appendCells` (`var word = UInt64(kind.packedCode) << cellKindShift; word |= UInt64(styleId) << cellStyleShift; ...`) and separately in `appendBlankCells`, and `cutTail` tests `cellWord(...) & PackedRetainedRow.Header.cellSpillBit` directly.

**Ideal fix.** Introduce a `CellWord` value over `UInt64` beside `LogicalLineRecord`, with `init(kind:styleId:scalarField:isSpill:)` and `@inline(__always)` `kind`, `styleId`, `scalarField`, `isSpill` accessors, and route every site above through it. The borrowed-pointer read loops stay as they are -- they simply wrap the loaded `UInt64`, which is free at -O.

**By construction.** It becomes impossible to read a cell field with the wrong shift or mask at one site while the others are right, and impossible for `appendCells` and `appendBlankCells` to disagree about the word's shape -- the layout is stated in exactly one place.

**Cheaper fallback.** Leave the constants where they are and add the four accessors as `@inline(__always)` private helpers on `LogicalLineStore`, routing the eight sites through them. Same reduction, but the encoding stays split across two types.

**Verification.** `TerminalRetainedRowReadPathTests` and the representation expectations in `TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests` already assert per-cell kind, scalars, and style through the public read walks at every retained position; they must stay green with no test edits.

**Risk.** The read loops in `withPaintedCells` and `forEachClosedRecordCell` are the measured frame path, so confirm the wrapper is fully inlined (it is a single-field frozen struct) rather than assuming it; a paired `just benchmark-quick` against the pre-change revision on a browse workload settles it if there is any doubt.

**Vetted.** Counted the sites in `LogicalLineStore.swift`: the kind decode `(word >> cellKindShift) & cellKindMask` appears at five places (`forEachClosedRecordCell`, `withPaintedCells`, `forEachKind`, `cell(recordIndex:recordOffset:record:cellOffset:)`, `cellKind(recordAt:cell:)`), the style extraction at four (including the spacer word in `withPaintedCells`), the scalar-field plus spill-bit test at three, and the write side is spelled twice (`appendCells`, `appendBlankCells`) with `cutTail` testing `cellSpillBit` directly. Every quote in the evidence is verbatim in the tree. The read loops are inside `withUnsafeBufferPointer` borrows over `ContiguousArray<UInt64>`, so a frozen single-field wrapper over the loaded `UInt64` costs nothing at -O; the risk note asking for that to be confirmed rather than assumed is the correct posture given the doc-28/doc-16 history in agent-docs/terminal-performance.md.

**Do after.** [STORE-1](#store-1), [STORE-2](#store-2)

<a id="store-4"></a>

##### STORE-4. State the open tail's scratch-table key base once, so a trimmed head cannot key it two ways

`correctness` &middot; impact 2, confidence 4 &middot; effort small &middot; wave 1 &middot; rescored

**Files.** `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#appendCells`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#hyperlinkId`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#loadOpenScratch`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#cutTail`

**Problem.** `HyperlinkEntry.offset` and `IdentityRun.start` carry a cell offset with no declared base, and the writers and readers disagree about which base that is once the head record has been trimmed. A head trim leaves the in-arena tables in place with their original keys (documented on `LogicalLineRecord.identityEntryCount`) and records the shift in `headTrimmedCells`, so the reader adds it back. The open-tail scratch is written without it.

**Evidence.** `appendCells` computes `let cellOffset = record.cellCount + index` -- `record.cellCount` is the header's count, which `trimHeadRecord` decrements via `trimmed.cellCount -= cut` -- then stores `HyperlinkEntry(offset: cellOffset, id: id)` and `IdentityRun(start: cellOffset, extent: 1, base: identity)`. The reader `cell(recordIndex:recordOffset:record:cellOffset:)` computes `let keyOffset = cellOffset + (recordIndex == 0 ? headTrimmedCells : 0)` and `hyperlinkId`/`contentIdentity` binary-search the open scratch for that `keyOffset`. `loadOpenScratch` refills the same arrays straight from the arena tables, whose keys are original-base. `cutTail` then filters them against a trimmed-base bound: `openHyperlinks.removeAll { $0.offset >= newCellCount }`. Reachability today is narrow -- the head record can only be the open tail when `offsets.count == 1`, and `forcedSplitCellCap` caps one record at 1/32 of the budget -- but nothing in the types or the code states that constraint.

**Ideal fix.** Make the base explicit and single: key the scratch by original cell offset everywhere, computed in one private accessor (the tail's key base, which is `headTrimmedCells` when the open record is also the head and 0 otherwise) used by `appendCells`, `loadOpenScratch`, `cutTail`, and `forEachHyperlinkId` alike. Better still, wrap it in a one-field `OriginalCellOffset` struct so a trimmed-relative count cannot be passed where a key is expected.

**By construction.** With a distinct offset type for the two bases, handing a trimmed-relative index to a table keyed by original offsets stops compiling, so the whole class of "the head trim rebased one side of a lookup" disappears rather than being argued unreachable.

**Cheaper fallback.** Assert the constraint that makes the mix unreachable -- `precondition(headTrimmedCells == 0 || offsets.count > 1)` in `trimHeadRecord` -- so the latent case fails loudly instead of silently misattributing a hyperlink id or a content identity.

**Verification.** Build a store at a budget where one logical line can be head-trimmed while still open, print a hyperlinked and content-identified run into it, evict one display row, append more cells, and assert `recordCells(at: 0)` reports the same `hyperlinkId`/`contentIdentity` per surviving cell as the untrimmed store did for the corresponding cells.

**Risk.** None to behavior in the currently reachable configurations; the change is confined to how the scratch entries are keyed. The main cost is deciding between the cheap precondition and the typed offset -- the precondition documents an accident, the type removes it.

**Vetted.** Verified the whole chain. `appendCells` keys scratch entries by `record.cellCount + index`, and `trimHeadRecord` does `trimmed.cellCount -= cut` while `LogicalLineRecord.identityEntryCount`'s doc comment states the in-arena tables keep their original keys. `loadOpenScratch` reads those original-base keys straight back out (`u16(entry)` for runs, `index` for the per-cell encoding), the reader `cell(recordIndex:recordOffset:record:cellOffset:)` adds `headTrimmedCells` for record 0, and `cutTail` filters `openHyperlinks.removeAll { $0.offset >= newCellCount }` against a trimmed-base bound. So three of the four sites are original-base and `appendCells` is trimmed-base -- the mismatch is exactly as described. What moves the score down is reachability: `headTrimmedCells > 0` on the *open* record requires `offsets.count == 1`, and `forcedSplitCellCount(forCapacity:)` caps one record at `(budget/32)/8` cells, so a single record plus its scratch cannot reach the budget that triggers `evictToBudget`. The only other eviction caller is the reserve loop in the admission path, which evicts when a contiguous run cannot be found -- narrow, geometry-dependent, and I could not construct it by reading alone. This is a latent type-safety defect with no demonstrated path, not a live bug.

**Sharper ideal.** Prefer the typed `OriginalCellOffset` half of the ideal over the "one private accessor" half: an accessor still lets a trimmed-relative count be passed to it, while a distinct type makes the mix a compile error, which is what the design bar asks for. Given the impact, the cheap `precondition(headTrimmedCells == 0 || offsets.count > 1)` in `trimHeadRecord` is a defensible first step -- but it documents an accident rather than removing it, and should be labelled as such in the plan.

<details>
<summary><b>Starter kit</b> -- current shape, 18 change sites, the tests, and the first failing test</summary>

**Current shape.** Inside `Terminal.LogicalLineStore` the open tail's side tables live outside the arena as `private var openHyperlinks: [HyperlinkEntry]` and `private var openIdentityRuns: [IdentityRun]`, where `HyperlinkEntry` is `{ var offset: Int; var id: Terminal.HyperlinkId }` and `IdentityRun` is `{ var start: Int; var extent: Int; var base: Terminal.ContentIdentity }` -- both `Int` fields carrying a cell offset whose base is nowhere declared. `private mutating func appendCells(_ cells: UnsafeBufferPointer<Terminal.GridCell>)` computes `let cellOffset = record.cellCount + index` and stores that, where `record.cellCount` is the header count that `trimHeadRecord` has already decremented (`trimmed.cellCount -= cut`), so the key is trimmed-relative. Every reader uses the original base instead: `private func cell(recordIndex:recordOffset:record:cellOffset:)` computes `let keyOffset = cellOffset + (recordIndex == 0 ? headTrimmedCells : 0)` and hands it to `private func hyperlinkId(record:at:keyOffset:)` and `private func contentIdentity(record:at:keyOffset:)`, which binary-search `openHyperlinks` / `openIdentityRuns` on it; `private mutating func loadOpenScratch(from:at:)` refills both arrays straight from the in-arena tables, whose keys are original-base by the rule stated on `LogicalLineRecord.identityEntryCount`; and `func forEachHyperlinkId(_:)` filters entries against `retainedStart = index == 0 ? headTrimmedCells : 0`. `private mutating func cutTail(to:from:at:)` is the odd fourth: it filters with `openHyperlinks.removeAll { $0.offset >= newCellCount }`, a trimmed-base bound. Code has not moved since the finding.

**Change sites.**

- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#HyperlinkEntry` -- Change `var offset: Int` to the new one-field `OriginalCellOffset` type (or, on the accessor-only variant, leave it and document the base). This is a private nested struct, so no ripple outside the file.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#IdentityRun` -- Same for `var start: Int`. `extent` stays a plain count -- it is a length, not an offset, and the type must not swallow it.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#appendCells` -- The bug site. `let cellOffset = record.cellCount + index` must become the original-base key -- `record.cellCount + index + openRecordKeyBase`, where the base is `headTrimmedCells` when the open record is also the head (`offsets.count == 1`) and 0 otherwise. Note this value is used twice more in the same loop, for the run-continuation test `open.start + open.extent == cellOffset`, so both uses move together.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#cutTail` -- `openHyperlinks.removeAll { $0.offset >= newCellCount }` and the two `openIdentityRuns` clamps (`last.start >= newCellCount`, `last.start + last.extent > newCellCount`) all compare a key against a trimmed-relative cell count. Rebase the bound to `newCellCount + keyBase`, or convert the bound into the offset type so the mismatch cannot be spelled.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#loadOpenScratch` -- No behavior change (it already reads original-base keys out of the arena), but every `IdentityRun(start: u16(entry) ...)` and `HyperlinkEntry(offset: u16(entry) ...)` construction, plus the per-cell branch that uses the loop `index` as `start`, needs the type wrapper applied. The per-cell branch is the one to check hardest: `index` there runs over `record.identityEntryCount`, which is the *original* count, so it is already original-base and must not be rebased.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#flushOpenTables` -- Writes `setU16(entry.offset, at: at)` and iterates `for run in openIdentityRuns` writing `run.start`. Once the scratch is original-base at every site this becomes correct by construction, but the calls need `.rawValue` (or equivalent) if the offset becomes a type. See the blockers note about `setU16` truncation.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#hyperlinkId` -- Signature `keyOffset: Int` becomes the offset type; the open-record binary search compares `entry.offset` against it, and the closed-record search compares `u16(entry)` against it.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#contentIdentity` -- Same signature change; the run arithmetic `run.base &+ Terminal.ContentIdentity(keyOffset - run.start)` needs a difference operator on the type, and the per-cell branch indexes the arena by `keyOffset * identityCellBytes`.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#cell(recordIndex:recordOffset:record:cellOffset:)` -- `let keyOffset = cellOffset + (recordIndex == 0 ? headTrimmedCells : 0)` becomes the single conversion from a retained-relative offset into the key type -- this is the one place the two bases are allowed to meet.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#forEachHyperlinkId` -- `retainedStart`/`retainedEnd` and the `entry.offset >= retainedStart && entry.offset < retainedEnd` filter move onto the offset type.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#trimHeadRecord` -- If the plan takes the cheap first step, this is where `precondition(headTrimmedCells == 0 || offsets.count > 1)` goes -- but note the constraint the finding wants asserted is about the *open* record, and `trimHeadRecord` can legitimately trim a closed head when `offsets.count == 1` too, so state the condition as "the head record is not also the open tail" rather than on record count alone.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#recordTextPosition` -- Computes `let originalOffset = cellOffset + (recordIndex == 0 ? headTrimmedCells : 0)` and stores it in `RecordTextPosition.cellOffset`. This is a *third* consumer of the same base, and `RecordTextPosition` is read outside the file. If the typed-offset route is taken, decide deliberately whether `RecordTextPosition.cellOffset` adopts the type or stays an `Int` at the boundary.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#position(of:)` -- `let retainedStart = low == 0 ? headTrimmedCells : 0` then `coordinate.cellOffset - retainedStart` -- the inverse conversion, and the same decision as above applies.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#contentRank` -- Same `retainedStart` / `relativeOffset` pair.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#independentContentRank` -- Same pair again, in the test oracle.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#closedContentUnitTotal` -- Builds a coordinate with `cellOffset: record.cellCount + (index == 0 ? headTrimmedCells : 0)` -- another hand-written conversion in the same family.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#closedRecordScan (ClosedRecordScan.cellOffsetBase)` -- `cellOffsetBase: recordIndex == 0 ? headTrimmedCells : 0` is published to callers so a scan can key coordinates arithmetically. Whatever type the keys get, this field must agree with it, and its consumers outside the store must be found.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#recordsEqual (the `index == 0, lhs.headTrimmedCells != rhs.headTrimmedCells` branch)` -- Falls back to a per-cell comparison when two stores' head trims differ and the head record has tables. It reads through `cell(recordIndex:cellOffset:)`, so it inherits the fix rather than needing one -- but it is the place to check that the fix did not change equality for a trimmed open head.

- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- truncatingIntoAForcedSplitRecordKeepsItsSideTablesReadable -- the `reopenTailRecordForTruncation` + `cutTail` path with hyperlinks and identities on every cell
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- fragmentedIdentityFallsBackPerCellWithoutLoss -- the per-cell identity encoding, which `loadOpenScratch`'s second branch reconstructs
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- equalitySeesEverySideTableValue -- the `headTrimmedCells`-aware equality branch
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- headTrimPreservesHeadRecordIdentity and recordCoordinateSurvivesHeadTrim -- the `recordTextPosition` / `position(of:)` base conversions across a trim
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- maintainedTotalsAndContentRanksAgreeWithRecountsAfterEveryMutation -- `contentRank` against `independentContentRank`, both of which do the same base conversion

**Tests that will need updating.** Expect these; they assert the thing being changed.

- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- none, if `RecordTextPosition.cellOffset` keeps its `Int` type -- no test constructs a `HyperlinkEntry` or an `IdentityRun`, and no test names `headTrimmedCells`
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- recordCoordinateStaysTwoWords -- asserts the coordinate's storage cost; if the typed offset is given to `RecordTextPosition.cellOffset`, confirm the wrapper is a frozen single-field struct so this stays true
- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift -- contentRanksUseOnlyBlockMetadata -- same caveat, it asserts a metadata width

**Write this test first.** Suite `Logical-line record arena` (`lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift`), new test "An open line that is head-trimmed keeps the hyperlink and identity of every cell printed after the trim". Scenario: `var store = Terminal.LogicalLineStore(budgetBytes: 1 << 16, width: 4)` -- a generous budget so nothing evicts on its own. Admit one soft-wrapped 8-cell row (two display rows) whose cells carry `hyperlinkId: 7` and stepping `contentIdentity` values, leaving record 0 open and alone in the store. Call the existing `evictOne(&store)` helper once: `evictOneDisplayRow` folds the first display row, `cut` (4) is less than `record.cellCount` (8), so `trimHeadRecord` runs on the *open* head -- `headTrimmedCells` becomes 4 and `record.cellCount` becomes 4. Now admit a second soft-wrapped row of four more hyperlinked, identified cells into the same open record. Assertion: `store.recordCells(at: 0)!` has 8 cells, every one reports `hyperlinkId == 7`, and their `contentIdentity` values are the contiguous run the admissions supplied. Why it fails today: `appendCells` keys the new entries at `record.cellCount + index` = 4..7 (trimmed base), while `cell(recordIndex:...)` looks them up at `cellOffset + headTrimmedCells` = 8..11 (original base), so the four newly printed cells come back with `hyperlinkId == nil` and `contentIdentity == nil` -- and the four surviving original cells, whose true keys are 4..7, are the ones that answer for offsets 4..7 instead, so identities are also misattributed. The finding calls this latent rather than live because a real terminal cannot reach a trimmed open head through `evictToBudget`; the test reaches it through the store's own `evictOneDisplayRow`, which is a supported member the suite already drives directly.

**Blockers and surprises.** Two real surprises. First, `setU16` truncates silently (`UInt16(truncatingIfNeeded: value)`), and `flushOpenTables` writes scratch keys through it. Today a scratch key can never exceed the record's cell count, which `forcedSplitCellCap` bounds at `(budget / 32) / 8` -- 65,536 at the 16 MiB budget, already one past what a `u16` field holds. Rebasing scratch keys to original offsets makes a trimmed-then-extended open record's keys grow past its own cell count, so the plan must state the bound explicitly and either add a precondition in `flushOpenTables` or show the cap keeps it under 65,535. Second, the scratch is not the only thing keyed here: `loadOpenScratch`'s per-cell branch uses the raw loop `index` over `record.identityEntryCount` as a run start, and `identityEntryCount` is documented on `LogicalLineRecord` as "**Never reduced by a head trim**, because the table stays where it is and keeps its original keys" -- so that index is already original-base and must not be rebased. Getting that backwards would break `fragmentedIdentityFallsBackPerCellWithoutLoss`. Beyond those, the change is confined to one file: `HyperlinkEntry` and `IdentityRun` are private, and nothing outside `LogicalLineStore.swift` names them.

**The preparer's read on the ideal fix.** The finding offers "one private accessor" and "a one-field `OriginalCellOffset` struct" as two halves of one ideal, and the audit's own Sharper ideal already prefers the type. Reading the code strengthens that: `headTrimmedCells` is converted by hand at *nine* sites, not the four the finding lists (`cell`, `recordTextPosition`, `position(of:)`, `contentRank`, `independentContentRank`, `closedContentUnitTotal`, `closedRecordScan`, `forEachHyperlinkId`, and the equality branch). An accessor removes the duplication at those nine but leaves every one of them free to hand a retained-relative `Int` to a key parameter. The type is what makes the class of defect unrepresentable, and the nine sites are what make it worth the ceremony. One caveat the finding does not raise: `RecordTextPosition.cellOffset` is an original-base offset that travels outside the store, so the typed route has to decide whether the type crosses that boundary too -- keeping it inside the store and converting at `recordTextPosition` / `position(of:)` is the smaller surface and probably right.

**Readiness: needs-decision.** A human should pick between the two shapes before an agent starts, because they are different amounts of work with different guarantees: (a) the typed `OriginalCellOffset`, which touches roughly seventeen sites and makes the mix a compile error, or (b) the cheap `precondition` in `trimHeadRecord` plus a one-line fix to `appendCells`, which documents the accident and pins the one bug. AGENTS.md's design bar says (a) is the ideal and (b) needs a stated reason. The failing test above is the same either way, so the test can be written before the decision lands.

</details>

<a id="store-5"></a>

##### STORE-5. Give a block one record-range accessor instead of five hand-copied index conversions

`simplification` &middot; impact 2, confidence 5 &middot; effort small &middot; wave 1 &middot; rescored

**Files.** `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#recomputeIndex`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#firstDisplayRow`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#contentRank`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#locate`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#independentContentBlockTotalsForTesting`

**Problem.** The mapping from a block index to the retained record indices it covers is written out five times. It is the store's trickiest arithmetic -- it must clamp the first block against `firstRecordSequence` because the head block is partially evicted, and the last against `offsets.count` -- and every reader that touches the block ring re-derives it. The oracle `independentContentBlockTotalsForTesting` re-derives it too, so it does not check that arithmetic independently of the code it is meant to check.

**Evidence.** `let first = max(firstRecordSequence, blockNumber * Self.blockSize) - firstRecordSequence` together with `let end = min(offsets.count, (blockNumber + 1) * Self.blockSize - firstRecordSequence)` appears verbatim in `recomputeIndex` and in `independentContentBlockTotalsForTesting`. The `first` half alone reappears as `blockFirst` in both `contentRank(of:)` and `firstDisplayRow(ofRecord:)`, and as `let firstSequence = max(firstRecordSequence, blockNumber * Self.blockSize)` in `locate(displayRow:)`. All five also independently compute `let blockIndex = sequence / Self.blockSize - firstBlockNumber` or its inverse.

**Ideal fix.** Add two private accessors -- `blockIndex(ofRecord:) -> Int?` and `recordRange(inBlock:) -> Range<Int>` -- and route all five sites through them. `recomputeIndex`, `contentRank`, `firstDisplayRow`, and `locate` then read as a block lookup plus a scan over a range, and the head-block clamp is stated once.

**By construction.** The head block's partial-eviction clamp stops being something each caller can get wrong: a caller can only ask a block which records it covers, so a site that forgets the `max(firstRecordSequence, ...)` clamp cannot be written.

**Cheaper fallback.** None -- the ideal fix is small.

**Verification.** Existing coverage carries this: `independentContentBlockTotalsForTesting` against `contentBlockTotalsForTesting`, `independentDisplayRowRecount` against `grandDisplayRowTotal`, and the `locate` / `position(ofRecord:cellOffset:)` round-trip expectations in `TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests` all fail if the range conversion changes meaning.

**Risk.** The one judgement call is the test oracle: routing `independentContentBlockTotalsForTesting` through the shared accessor weakens it as an independent check, so keep that site spelled out and say why in its comment.

**Vetted.** All five sites are in the tree verbatim: `recomputeIndex` and `independentContentBlockTotalsForTesting` carry the identical `first`/`end` pair, `contentRank(of:)` and `firstDisplayRow(ofRecord:)` carry the identical `blockFirst` clamp, and `locate(displayRow:)` carries `let firstSequence = max(firstRecordSequence, blockNumber * Self.blockSize)`. `let blockIndex = sequence / Self.blockSize - firstBlockNumber` is independently written at four more places (`contentRank`, `firstDisplayRow`, `addContentUnits(_:toBlockContaining:)`, and the block accessor near the tail of the file). The duplication is real and the accessor pair is obviously right. Scored down because no defect was found in any of the five copies, they are all in one file within ~1,800 lines of each other, and the risk section already concedes that one of the five (the test oracle) should stay spelled out -- so the fix dedupes four sites, not five.

<details>
<summary><b>Starter kit</b> -- current shape, 11 change sites, the tests, and the first failing test</summary>

**Current shape.** `Terminal.LogicalLineStore` keeps its cached row and content totals in `private var blocks: RingBuffer<Block>`, one `Block` per `static let blockSize = 64` records, indexed against `private var firstRecordSequence: Int` and the derived `private var firstBlockNumber: Int { firstRecordSequence / Self.blockSize }`. Two conversions are written out by hand all over the file: sequence-to-block-index, spelled `let blockIndex = sequence / Self.blockSize - firstBlockNumber`, and block-index-to-record-range, spelled as the pair `let first = max(firstRecordSequence, blockNumber * Self.blockSize) - firstRecordSequence` and `let end = min(offsets.count, (blockNumber + 1) * Self.blockSize - firstRecordSequence)`. The `max` is the head-block clamp -- the oldest block is partially evicted, so its first covered record is not at a block boundary. Nothing here has moved since the finding; `1c6bcf1f` is the newest commit on the file and it touched the grand totals, not the block ring.

**Change sites.**

- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#LogicalLineStore` -- Add the two private accessors next to `firstBlockNumber`, where the derived-block-number comment already lives: `private func blockIndex(ofRecord recordIndex: Int) -> Int?` (nil when the block ring does not cover it, which is what four of the call sites currently guard by hand) and `private func recordRange(inBlock blockIndex: Int) -> Range<Int>` carrying the head-block clamp. Give each a `///` comment stating the clamp as the invariant.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#recomputeIndex` -- Replace the `blockNumber` / `first` / `end` triple with `for recordIndex in recordRange(inBlock: blockIndex)`.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#contentRank` -- Replace `let blockIndex = sequence / Self.blockSize - firstBlockNumber` plus its `guard blockIndex >= 0, blockIndex < blocks.count` with `guard let blockIndex = blockIndex(ofRecord: index)`, and replace the `blockFirst` clamp with `recordRange(inBlock: blockIndex).lowerBound`. Keep the `Instrument.searchDistanceWork.record()` call inside the scan loop.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#firstDisplayRow` -- Same two replacements. This one currently returns 0 on a miss rather than nil, so preserve that behavior deliberately rather than letting the optional accessor change it.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#locate` -- Replace `let blockNumber = firstBlockNumber + blockIndex` / `let firstSequence = max(firstRecordSequence, blockNumber * Self.blockSize)` / `var recordIndex = firstSequence - firstRecordSequence` with `var recordIndex = recordRange(inBlock: blockIndex).lowerBound`. Note the scan loop below runs to `offsets.count`, not to the range's upper bound -- that is deliberate (a row may fall in the next block if the index is stale), so do not tighten it while you are in there.
- `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/LogicalLineStore.swift#addContentUnits(_:toBlockContaining:)` -- The fourth independent copy of the sequence-to-block-index conversion, with a `precondition` instead of a guard. Decide whether it reads better as `blockIndex(ofRecord:) == nil`; it is a judgement call, not a required site.

**Write this test first.** There is no new failing test. This is a pure refactor: the accessors must return exactly what the five hand-written copies return today, and no copy has a defect (the audit's Vetted note says so explicitly, and re-reading them confirms it -- all five carry the `max(firstRecordSequence, ...)` clamp and the `min(offsets.count, ...)` bound). Writing a test that asserts the accessors exist or are called would assert the structure of a private helper, which AGENTS.md forbids. The characterization test is `maintainedTotalsAndContentRanksAgreeWithRecountsAfterEveryMutation` in `lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalLogicalLineStoreTests.swift`: it drives every mutation that moves the block ring and checks the maintained per-block content totals, the grand row total and every retained coordinate's rank against independent recounts, and it is the test that fails if the clamp changes meaning at any of the four sites being routed through the accessor. Run it, plus `truncatingAcrossABlockBoundaryKeepsEveryRowAddressable` and `forwardCursorWalksWithOneLocate`, before and after.

**Blockers and surprises.** One thing that makes it easier than the finding admits and one that makes it slightly harder. Harder: `blockIndex(ofRecord:)` has three different miss behaviors across its callers -- `contentRank` returns nil, `firstDisplayRow` returns 0, and `addContentUnits(_:toBlockContaining:)` traps on a `precondition`. An optional-returning accessor is the right shape, but each call site must keep its own miss behavior rather than inheriting one; silently changing `firstDisplayRow`'s 0 into a nil would change `position(ofRecord:cellOffset:)`'s result. Also note `locate`'s in-block scan deliberately runs past the block's upper bound to `offsets.count`, with a comment above the search explaining that a block claiming no row is treated as a stale index rather than a lookup elsewhere -- do not let `recordRange` tempt a tightening there. Nothing else: the accessors are private, `Block` is private, `blockSize` is internal and read by one test as a fixture size only, and no file outside `LogicalLineStore.swift` touches the block ring.

#### Area: Selection, search, damage, presentation (`INTERACT`)

_Scope: Terminal selection, search, hit-testing, damage, and presentation snapshotting_

**The auditor's read on the area.** The area is in good shape: `TerminalDamage`'s word-backed representation, `NeedleWindow`'s position-generic matcher, `TerminalSearchStatus`'s "no invalid counter" enum, and the pinned-range selection drag are all careful, well-documented designs. The findings below are all about facts that still have two owners or two spellings: one damage-composition rule written twice, one search-index refresh that must be pushed from seven call sites, one pointer-cell value that is destructured before it crosses the policy seam, and one selection mutation whose granularity travels beside it instead of inside it. I did not audit the render planner (`RenderFramePlanner`, `SearchMatchRenderPlanning`), `TerminalInputEncoding`, or `LogicalLineStore`, and I ran no builds or tests -- every claim is from reading the cited code.

<a id="interact-1"></a>

##### INTERACT-1. Refresh the search index through one history-mutation funnel instead of seven hand-placed calls

`structural` &middot; impact 4, confidence 5 &middot; effort medium &middot; wave 1 &middot; confirmed

**Files.** `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/Terminal.swift#synchronizeSearchIndexPrefix`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/TerminalSearch.swift#synchronizeIndex`, `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/TerminalSearch.swift#resolvedSearchMatchRange`

**Problem.** `Terminal.Search` retains match endpoints as `LogicalLineStore.RecordTextPosition` values, which stop resolving the moment history changes which records it owns. Keeping them valid is a pushed obligation: every site that evicts, truncates, closes, or reopens a record must remember to call `synchronizeSearchIndexPrefix()`. There are seven such calls today, in unrelated code paths (budget enforcement, ED 3, two resize tail-pulls, wrap-claim sever, wrap-claim restore, a test helper), and nothing makes a new history mutation call it. The failure is not a stale highlight: a retained coordinate whose record retired reaches `preconditionFailure("the search index retained a retired record coordinate")`, which traps the process.

**Evidence.** `synchronizeSearchIndexPrefix()` appears at seven separate call sites in `Terminal.swift` (inside `enforceScrollbackBudget`, the ED 3 branch that calls `history.removeAll()`, both `history.truncateTail(displayRows:)` resize paths, `severScrollbackWrapClaim`, `restoreWrapClaimBeforeCursor`, and `evictScrollbackRowsForTesting`). It is the only thing that trims `index.prefixMatches` and rebuilds `index.boundaryWindow`. `Search.resolvedSearchMatchRange` then does `guard let start = context.history.position(of: match.start), let end = ... else { preconditionFailure("the search index retained a retired record coordinate") }` -- so a missed synchronize is a trap, not a wrong answer.

**Ideal fix.** Make `history` private to one mutating funnel on `Terminal` -- e.g. `mutating func withHistory<R>(_ body: (inout LogicalLineStore) -> R) -> R` that runs `search?.synchronizeIndex(with: history)` on the way out -- and route every record-ownership mutation through it. `synchronizeIndex` already early-returns after comparing two cheap values (`retainedStart`, `indexedThroughRecord`), so the funnel costs a nil check when no search is active. A mutation site that forgets to refresh then does not compile, because there is no other way to reach the store.

**By construction.** "A history mutation that changes record ownership without refreshing the retained search index" becomes unrepresentable -- and with it the `preconditionFailure` on a retired record coordinate, which no longer has a reachable cause.

**Cheaper fallback.** Keep the pushed calls but have `LogicalLineStore` expose a monotone record-ownership counter, and assert in `searchContext` that the counter the index last saw equals the store's -- turning a silent trap deep in a read into a loud failure next to the missed site. This is strictly worse: it detects the omission instead of preventing it.

**Verification.** Behavioral test: begin a search whose matches sit in the oldest retained records, then drive each history-mutating path (feed past the scrollback budget, `ESC[3J`, narrow-then-widen resize so the tail is pulled back, a wrap-claim sever) and assert after each that `searchStatus` still reports the surviving matches and that `activeSearchMatchRange` resolves. Add one test that mutates history through the new funnel with a deliberately missing manual refresh and shows the counts still agree. `swift test --package-path lib/TerminalCore --filter Search`.

**Risk.** The funnel must not force a copy of the copy-on-write store: it has to hand out `inout` access exactly as today's direct mutation does, or the arena gets copied per mutation. Verify with the existing throughput benchmark before and after.

**Vetted.** All seven `synchronizeSearchIndexPrefix()` call sites exist exactly as listed in `Terminal.swift` (`evictScrollbackRowsForTesting`, `enforceScrollbackBudget`, the ED 3 `history.removeAll()` arm, both resize `history.truncateTail(displayRows:)` paths, `severScrollbackWrapClaim`, and the wrap-claim restore), and `TerminalSearch.swift#resolvedSearchMatchRange` really does end in `preconditionFailure("the search index retained a retired record coordinate")` when `history.position(of:)` returns nil. `searchContext` builds a fresh `Search.Context` from `history` with no lazy synchronize, so a mutation that retires a record and skips the push is a trap on the next read, not a stale highlight. `synchronizeIndex` early-returns after comparing `retainedStart` and `indexedThroughRecord`, so the funnel is cheap as the finding claims.

**Correction.** One claim in **By construction** needs weakening as written: `history` is a `private var` on `Terminal`, and every mutation site is inside the ~7,500-line `Terminal.swift`, where `private` does not bind. A funnel declared next to the property therefore does not make the omission a compile error -- a later method can still write `history.foo()` directly. To get the by-construction claim, the store has to sit behind a small wrapper type declared in a *different* file whose stored property is private there, with `withMutation` as the only mutating door. That is still the ideal fix; it is just one more file than the finding implies.

**Conflicts with.** [FIND-1](#find-1)

**Current shape.** `Terminal` is one ~7,600-line struct in `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/Terminal.swift`. It holds `private var history: LogicalLineStore` (assigned in `init`, no default) plus a sibling `private var historyEvictionsObserved = 0` high-water mark, and `private mutating func synchronizeSearchIndexPrefix()` which early-returns when `search == nil` and otherwise does `let retainedHistory = history; search?.synchronizeIndex(with: retainedHistory)` (the local copy exists so the store is not both `inout` on `self` and an argument). Search lives in `lib/TerminalCore/Sources/TerminalCore/TerminalSearch.swift` as `extension Terminal { struct Search }` with `mutating func synchronizeIndex(with history: LogicalLineStore)`, which early-returns after comparing `retainedStart` (`history.recordTextPosition(recordIndex: 0, cellOffset: 0)`) and `indexedThrough` (`history.recordIdentity(at: closedCount - 1)`) against the values the index last saw, and `private func resolvedSearchMatchRange(_:in:context:)`, which ends in `preconditionFailure("the search index retained a retired record coordinate")` when `context.history.position(of:)` returns nil. Reads build `Search.Context(history:projection:evictedRowCount:columnCount:)` fresh from `Terminal.searchContext` with no lazy synchronize. Everything the finding describes is in the tree verbatim; nothing has moved (last touch of TerminalSearch.swift is `9f0742c3 refactor(terminal): lift search into its own subsystem`).

The wrapper struct must live in a NEW file in the same module, with its `LogicalLineStore` stored property `private` there and a single `mutating func withMutation<R>(_ body: (inout LogicalLineStore) -> R) -> R` door plus non-mutating read forwarding.

- lib/TerminalCore/Tests/TerminalCoreTests/TerminalSearchTests.swift -- head eviction cost is unchanged by retained match density -- asserts `dense == empty` and `dense <= 2` on the same instrument. This is the tightest bound in the suite and the first thing a per-row funnel breaks.
