No ADR constrains this file, no generated file is involved, and nothing in `app/` or `lib/TerminalPTY` touches the storage.

**The preparer's read on the ideal fix.** The finding's stated ideal covers both the pointer owners and the wheel remainders. Only the pointer half is real, and the audit's own Correction says so -- the three wheel accessors are exhaustive switches, so the compiler already enforces what the finding says a developer must remember. Doing the wheel half would replace compile-time exhaustiveness with a runtime keyed lookup, which is strictly worse by the design bar. Implement the pointer half only. Second, the finding's risk note warns that a `Dictionary` would make `TerminalInteractionState` refcounted on a hot path -- but the storage today is an `Array`, which is already heap-allocated and refcounted, so any of the candidate stores (a Dictionary keyed by the button, or a fixed-size inline struct) is neutral or better than the status quo. That risk is smaller than the finding admits, and an inline store is a small free win rather than a defensive compromise.

**Readiness: ready.** An agent can start on this from the above.

</details>

#### Area: Core reducer (Update/Msg/Command) (`REDUCE`)

_Scope: The pure Elm reducer and its message/command vocabulary (lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift, Msg.swift, Command.swift, CoreEnvironment.swift, ReconcileFollowUps.swift, PaneLifecycle*.swift)_

**The auditor's read on the area.** The reducer is disciplined in the large: one chokepoint `defer` runs the four repair passes, `Command` is genuinely free of projection cases, and every `Command` case has exactly one consumer in `AppRuntime.perform`. The weak spots are all in the middle layer: a pending-confirmation record whose four optionals are validated by hand instead of by type, one Msg/Command pair that launders model state through the view and back, and a "clear the focused pane's alerts" rule copied into nine arms with two arms that quietly disagree. I did not audit IpcDispatch.swift, ModelOperations.swift, or Model.swift beyond the declarations the reducer arms depend on, nor the app-side reconcile passes except where a finding proposes moving work into one.

<a id="reduce-1"></a>

##### REDUCE-1. Make PendingConfirmation an enum so a subject cannot carry the wrong payload

**Merged into [MODEL-1](#model-1).** Track the work under MODEL-1.

`structural` &middot; impact 4, confidence 5 &middot; effort medium &middot; confirmed

**Files.** `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Model.swift#PendingConfirmation`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#confirmPendingConfirmation`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#chooseDeleteGroupConfirmation`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#reconcilePendingConfirmation`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/ModelOperations.swift#emitConfirmation`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#emitDeleteGroupConfirmation`

**Problem.** `PendingConfirmation` is a flat struct of `subject` plus three optionals (`tabTitle`, `impact`, `deleteGroup`) whose validity is entirely a function of `subject`. Which optionals must be present, and which message may act on the record, is re-checked by hand in four places, and three of those checks answer an invalid combination by silently returning `[]` -- the shape a user sees as a confirmation panel that does nothing when clicked.

**Evidence.** `PendingConfirmation` declares `let subject: ConfirmationSubject; let tabTitle: DisplayLine?; let impact: CloseImpact?; let deleteGroup: DeleteGroupConfirmation?`. `emitConfirmation` builds `.app` with `impact: nil, deleteGroup: nil`, close subjects with `impact: impact, deleteGroup: nil`, and `emitDeleteGroupConfirmation` builds `.deleteGroup` with `impact: nil` plus a non-nil `deleteGroup`. Nothing stops `.tab` + non-nil `deleteGroup`, or `.deleteGroup` + nil `deleteGroup`. The consumers pay for it: `confirmPendingConfirmation` opens with `if case .deleteGroup = pending.subject { return [] }` and then still needs `case .deleteGroup: return []` arms in both of its switches; `chooseDeleteGroupConfirmation` guards `case .deleteGroup(let groupId) = pending.subject, let frozen = pending.deleteGroup` and drops the click if either half is missing; `closeSubjectHasGrown` starts with `guard let snapshot = pending.impact ... else { return false }`, so a close confirmation built without an impact silently loses its grown-subject re-prompt.

**Ideal fix.** Replace the struct with an enum that carries exactly the payload its case needs: `case quit(id:)`, `case close(id:, subject: CloseSubject, tabTitle: DisplayLine?, impact: CloseImpact, quitAuthorized: Bool)`, `case deleteGroup(id:, groupId: GroupId, frozen: DeleteGroupConfirmation)`. Split `ConfirmationSubject` so `CloseSubject` holds only pane/tab/tabs. Then `Msg.confirmConfirmation` matches only the quit and close cases and `Msg.chooseDeleteGroupConfirmation` only the delete-group case, and every `return []` for an impossible combination disappears.

**By construction.** A pending confirmation whose payload does not match its subject -- a delete-group transaction with no frozen destination, a close transaction with no impact snapshot, a quit transaction carrying an impact -- becomes unrepresentable, and with it the class of "the confirmation panel is up but the button does nothing".

**Cheaper fallback.** Keep the struct but give it a private init per subject and a `switch`-returning accessor that returns the payload bundle, so at least construction cannot produce an invalid pair. This still lets a reader construct a mismatched record inside the module.

**Verification.** Existing behavioral tests must keep passing: confirming a close whose subject grew re-prompts; choosing "move tabs" on a delete-group confirmation whose destination group vanished re-emits a fresh confirmation. Add one behavioral test that a delete-group confirmation answered by the plain confirm path is impossible to send (it no longer compiles) -- expressed as a test that the delete-group choice message is the only way the group is deleted.

**Risk.** Touches every construction and consumption site of the confirmation record plus the app-side `reconcileConfirmation` reader, so the panel's rendering switch must be re-derived from the new cases.

**Vetted.** Read `Model.swift#PendingConfirmation` (it is `id`, `subject`, `tabTitle?`, `impact?`, `deleteGroup?`, `quitAuthorized`), `ModelOperations.swift#emitConfirmation`, and all four consumers in Update.swift. Every quoted line is there: `confirmPendingConfirmation` opens with `if case .deleteGroup = pending.subject { return [] }` and still carries `case .deleteGroup: return []` inside its switch, `chooseDeleteGroupConfirmation` guards `case .deleteGroup(let groupId) = pending.subject, let frozen = pending.deleteGroup` and silently drops the click if either half is missing, and `closeSubjectHasGrown` returns `false` when `pending.impact` is nil. The merge into MODEL-1 is right -- same defect, same fix, and MODEL-1 covers the read sites this one omits.

**Do after.** [MODEL-1](#model-1)

**Conflicts with.** [CHROME-2](#chrome-2)

<a id="reduce-2"></a>

##### REDUCE-2. Let .startSearch open the pane's search state directly instead of round-tripping through the view

`structural` &middot; impact 3, confidence 5 &middot; effort small &middot; wave 2 &middot; rewritten

**Files.** `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#update`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Command.swift#Command`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Msg.swift#Msg`, `app/SwiftTerminalSessionView.swift#startSearch`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/TerminalBackendBoundary.swift`

**Problem.** Opening search is a decision the reducer already made, but the reducer does not record it. It emits a command, the runtime calls into the view, and the view immediately emits a message back that makes the reducer write the state it could have written in the first place. No information is gained on the trip, and the message's only parameter is always the same constant, leaving a dead branch in the reducer.

**Evidence.** `case .startSearch` returns `[.sendStartSearch(paneId: tab.paneTree.focusedPaneId)]`. `AppRuntime.perform` maps it to `paneSession(for: paneId)?.startSearch()`, whose entire body is `callbackGate.emit(.searchStarted(""))` (its comment even says "`.searchStarted` is what creates the pane's searchState"). That callback becomes `Msg.searchStarted(paneId:needle:)`, whose arm creates `model.searchState[paneId] = SearchModel()` and sets `focusOwner = .field`. It is the only emitter in the tree, so the arm's `if !needle.isEmpty { model.searchState[paneId]?.needle = needle }` branch can never run.

**Ideal fix.** Have `case .startSearch` write `model.searchState[paneId] = SearchModel()` with `focusOwner = .field` and return no command. The overlay already mounts from `model.searchState` via `reconcilePaneChrome` and the responder already moves via `reconcilePaneFocus`, so `Command.sendStartSearch`, `Msg.searchStarted`, the `TerminalBackendBoundary` mapping, and `SwiftTerminalSessionView.startSearch()` all delete.

**By construction.** There is no longer a moment where the reducer has decided search is open and the model does not say so, so no message ordering can drop or duplicate the opening; and a `searchStarted` report that disagrees with the reducer's own decision cannot be expressed.

**Cheaper fallback.** Keep the command but drop the `needle` parameter from `Msg.searchStarted` so the dead branch goes away. This leaves the round trip -- and with it the window where the model says search is closed while the view is opening it.

**Verification.** Behavioral test at the reducer: send `.startSearch` to a model with a selected tab and assert `model.searchState[focusedPaneId]` exists with `focusOwner == .field` and that no command is returned. UI-level check via `just test-ui` that Cmd-F still mounts the overlay and puts the caret in the field.

**Risk.** If any engine path other than `startSearch()` was expected to open the overlay later (none exists today), it would need its own message; the search-needle and end-search commands stay as they are.

**Vetted.** Confirmed the whole loop end to end: `Update.swift` `case .startSearch` returns `[.sendStartSearch(paneId: tab.paneTree.focusedPaneId)]`; `AppRuntime.perform` maps it to `paneSession(for:)?.startSearch()`; `SwiftTerminalSessionView#startSearch` is one line, `callbackGate.emit(.searchStarted(""))`, with the comment the finding quotes; `TerminalBackendBoundary` turns that into `Msg.searchStarted(paneId:needle:)`. It is the only emitter in app/, lib/, or ios/, so the arm's `if !needle.isEmpty` branch is dead outside tests. The problem is real. What the finding gets wrong is the fix: the current arm creates a `SearchModel` only when none exists, so pressing Cmd-F while search is already open keeps the typed needle and only reclaims field ownership (pinned by `UpdateSearchTests#searchStartedWhileActiveUpdatesNeedleAndOwner`). Writing `model.searchState[paneId] = SearchModel()` as stated would wipe the needle on a second Cmd-F.

**Correction.** The round trip is real and the deletion is right, but the reducer arm must reproduce today's re-entry behavior, not replace it: `.startSearch` should create `model.searchState[paneId]` only when it is nil, then set `focusOwner = .field`, and return no command. That preserves "Cmd-F while search is open re-focuses the field and keeps the needle". `Command.sendStartSearch`, `Msg.searchStarted`, the `TerminalBackendBoundary.searchStarted` mapping, `SwiftTerminalSessionView.startSearch()`, and the `TerminalSession` protocol requirement all delete. `UpdateSearchTests#startSearchEmitsSendStartSearchForFocusedPane` and the three tests that drive `.searchStarted` directly have to be rewritten to drive `.startSearch`, including one that asserts a second `.startSearch` leaves the needle intact.

**Conflicts with.** [MODEL-5](#model-5)

<a id="reduce-3"></a>

##### REDUCE-3. Repair the focused pane's alerts in one pass instead of copying the rule into nine arms

`structural` &middot; impact 3, confidence 4 &middot; effort medium &middot; wave 4 &middot; rewritten

**Files.** `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#update`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#applySelectTab`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#navigateToPane`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#closePaneBody`

**Problem.** "Under `alertClearMode == .focus`, the focused pane of the selected tab has no unread alerts" is an invariant, but it is enforced by nine hand-written copies of the same two lines at the arms that happen to move focus. Arms that move focus by another route were missed, so the model can sit in a state that violates the rule with nothing to repair it.

**Evidence.** `if model.config.alertClearMode == .focus { markAlertsReadForPane(...) }` appears nine times in Update.swift: in `.movePaneToTab`, `.movePaneToNewTab`, `.focusDirection`, `.paneBecameFirstResponder`, `.searchFieldBecameFirstResponder`, `.appBecameActive`, and in `closePaneBody`, `applySelectTab`, `navigateToPane`. Two of them disagree with the rest: `.movePaneToTab` and `.movePaneToNewTab` set `model.selectedTabId = targetTabId` directly and then clear alerts for the *moved* pane, not for the newly selected tab's `paneTree.focusedPaneId`. So dragging a pane into a tab whose focused pane holds an unread alert selects that tab and leaves the badge lit, while reaching the same tab through `.selectTab` clears it.

**Ideal fix.** Add `reconcileFocusedPaneAlerts(&model)` to the `defer` block at the top of `update()`, beside `reconcileTabState`: when `config.alertClearMode == .focus` and `model.isAppActive`, mark alerts read for `selectedTab(in: model)?.paneTree.focusedPaneId`. Delete all nine call sites. The `isAppActive` condition is what keeps a bell raised for the focused pane while the app is in the background unread -- the behavior `.sessionBell` and `desktopAlertCommands` already rely on -- and it makes `.appBecameActive`'s copy fall out for free.

**By construction.** A model in which focus-clear mode is on, the app is active, and the focused pane still has an unread alert stops being reachable, so "this arm forgot to clear alerts" ceases to be a possible defect.

**Cheaper fallback.** Route `.movePaneToTab` and `.movePaneToNewTab` through `applySelectTab` so at least every selection change clears the same pane. The nine copies remain, so the next arm that moves focus can miss it again.

**Verification.** Behavioral test: with `alertClearMode == .focus`, raise an unread alert on tab B's focused pane, then send `.movePaneToTab` moving a pane from tab A into tab B; assert no unread alert remains for tab B's focused pane -- and that the same holds after `.selectTab`, `.focusDirection`, and a last-pane `.closePane` that moves focus.

**Risk.** The `isAppActive` condition is a deliberate behavior choice: today a focus change while the app is inactive clears alerts, and after the fix it would not. Worth confirming with the user, since it changes what the dock badge shows after a background IPC navigate.

**Vetted.** The nine copies of `if model.config.alertClearMode == .focus { markAlertsReadForPane(...) }` are all there (`.movePaneToTab`, `.movePaneToNewTab`, `.focusDirection`, `.paneBecameFirstResponder`, `.searchFieldBecameFirstResponder`, `.appBecameActive`, `closePaneBody`, `applySelectTab`, `navigateToPane`). But the finding's headline evidence is wrong. `PaneTree.adopt` ends with `focusedPaneId = pane.id`, so in `.movePaneToTab` the moved pane *is* the target tab's focused pane; in `.movePaneToNewTab` path A the source tab is a single leaf holding that pane, and in path B the new tab holds only it. All three arms therefore clear alerts for exactly the newly selected tab's focused pane, the same pane `applySelectTab` would clear. There is no disagreement and no lit-badge bug there. A real miss does exist, one the finding did not look at: `closeTabRemoval` selects a fallback tab with a bare `model.selectedTabId = newId` and never clears alerts, so closing the selected tab leaves the next tab's focused pane badged, while reaching the same tab through `.selectTab` clears it.

**Correction.** The invariant "under `alertClearMode == .focus` the selected tab's focused pane has no unread alerts" is enforced by nine hand-written copies, and one path that changes the selection does not carry a copy: `Update.swift#closeTabRemoval` writes `model.selectedTabId = newId` for the fallback tab after removing the closed one, with no `markAlertsReadForPane`. Closing the selected tab therefore leaves the newly selected tab's focused pane showing an unread badge that selecting the same tab by hand would have cleared. (The `.movePaneToTab` / `.movePaneToNewTab` arms named in the original evidence are *not* a second instance: `PaneTree.adopt` sets `focusedPaneId` to the adopted pane, and both new-tab paths give the moved pane the whole tree, so the pane they clear is the newly selected tab's focused pane.) The ideal fix stands: one `reconcileFocusedPaneAlerts(&model)` in the `defer` block beside `reconcileTabState`, gated on `config.alertClearMode == .focus && model.isAppActive`, clearing for `selectedTab(in: model)?.paneTree.focusedPaneId`, with all nine copies deleted. The `isAppActive` gate is still a deliberate behavior change worth confirming with the user: today `.paneBecameFirstResponder` and `.focusDirection` clear alerts whether or not the app is active.

<details>
<summary><b>Starter kit</b> -- current shape, 13 change sites, the tests, and the first failing test</summary>

**Current shape.** `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#update(_ model: inout AppModel, _ msg: Msg, env: CoreEnv = .live) -> [Command]` opens with a `defer` block that calls, in order, `reconcileTabState(&model)`, `reconcileTodoPopover(&model)`, `reconcilePendingConfirmation(&model, env: env)`, `reconcileSidebarRenameTarget(&model)` -- with a long comment explaining that this is the single chokepoint for repairs that would otherwise be sprinkled across arms. Nine sites then hand-write `if model.config.alertClearMode == .focus { markAlertsReadForPane(paneId, in: &model) }`: in the arms `.movePaneToTab`, `.movePaneToNewTab`, `.focusDirection`, `.paneBecameFirstResponder`, `.searchFieldBecameFirstResponder`, `.appBecameActive`, and in the private helpers `closePaneBody`, `applySelectTab`, `navigateToPane`. `markAlertsReadForPane(_ paneId: PaneId, in model: inout AppModel) -> Bool` is `private` and `@discardableResult`; it flips `isUnread` on every alert for that pane. `AppModel.isAppActive` defaults to `true`. `reconcileTabState` lives in ModelOperations.swift, so a sibling `reconcileFocusedPaneAlerts` most naturally goes there too -- but `markAlertsReadForPane` is private to Update.swift, so one of the two has to move.

**Change sites.**

- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#update (the `defer` block)` -- Add `reconcileFocusedPaneAlerts(&model)` beside `reconcileTabState`. Order matters: it must run *after* `reconcileTabState`, because that pass can repair `selectedTabId` and the alert repair reads the selected tab.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/ModelOperations.swift (new `reconcileFocusedPaneAlerts`, beside `reconcileTabState` and `reconcileTodoPopover`)` -- New function: when `model.config.alertClearMode == .focus && model.isAppActive`, mark alerts read for `selectedTab(in: model)?.paneTree.focusedPaneId`. It needs `markAlertsReadForPane`, which is currently `private` in Update.swift -- either move that helper to ModelOperations.swift (it is a pure model operation and belongs there) or keep the new pass in Update.swift.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift (the `.movePaneToTab` arm)` -- Delete the focus-mode clear for the moved pane. Safe: `PaneTree.adopt` ends with `focusedPaneId = pane.id`, so the moved pane *is* the target tab's focused pane and the arm sets `model.selectedTabId = targetTabId` -- the reconcile clears the same pane.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift (the `.movePaneToNewTab` arm)` -- Delete the copy. Both paths give the moved pane the whole new tree and select it.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift (the `.focusDirection` arm)` -- Delete the copy; the arm's `updateSelectedTab { $0.paneTree.focus(target) }` is what the reconcile reads.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift (the `.paneBecameFirstResponder` arm)` -- Delete the copy inside the `if paneId != tab.paneTree.focusedPaneId` branch. The surrounding fence (`allPaneIds(tab.paneTree.root).contains(paneId)`) must stay -- it stops a background pane from moving this tab's focus at all.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift (the `.searchFieldBecameFirstResponder` arm)` -- Delete the copy. Same fence applies.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift (the `.appBecameActive` arm)` -- Delete the whole `if model.config.alertClearMode == .focus, let focusedPaneId = ...` block. The arm sets `model.isAppActive = true` before the defer runs, so the reconcile does exactly this work.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#closePaneBody` -- Delete `if removal.focusMoved, model.config.alertClearMode == .focus, tab.id == model.selectedTabId { markAlertsReadForPane(paneTree.focusedPaneId, ...) }`. Careful: this site clears *before* `updateTab(tab.id, in: &model) { tab.paneTree = paneTree }` writes the new tree back. The reconcile runs after the arm returns, so it sees the written tree -- confirm the write happens on every path out of this helper.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#applySelectTab` -- Delete the copy after `model.selectedTabId = id`. Keep the `.focusSession(focused: false)` loop (that is REDUCE-4's territory, not this one).
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#navigateToPane` -- Delete `if focusChanged && model.config.alertClearMode == .focus { markAlertsReadForPane(paneId, ...) }`. Note this helper calls `update(&model, .selectTab(...))` recursively, so the nested call already runs a full defer; the outer defer runs again after the focus write. Both converge on the same pane.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#closeTabRemoval` -- No code added here -- but this is the site the Vetted note identifies as the actual live defect: it writes `model.selectedTabId = newId` for the fallback tab with no alert clear. The reconcile fixes it for free, and this is what the first failing test targets.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#markAlertsReadForPane` -- May need to lose `private` (or move to ModelOperations.swift) depending on where the new pass lands.

**Tests that must keep passing.** These are the safety net.

- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateTabTests.swift -- testSelectTabFocusModeMarksFocusedPaneAlertsRead -- the canonical focus-mode selection test; `isAppActive` defaults to true so it stays green
- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateTabTests.swift -- testSelectTabFocusModeMarksAlertReadInCollapsedGroup
- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateLifecycleTests.swift -- testAppBecameActiveMarksFocusedPaneAlertReadInFocusMode -- the arm sets isAppActive = true before the defer, so the deleted copy is covered by the pass
- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateLifecycleTests.swift -- testAppBecameActiveDoesNotMarkReadInManualMode
- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateLifecycleTests.swift -- testAppBecameActiveLeavesBackgroundPaneAlertUnread -- pins that the pass touches only the *selected* tab's focused pane
- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdatePaneTests.swift -- testPaneBecameFirstResponderLeavesAlertUnreadInManualMode
- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdatePaneTests.swift -- the two-leg closePane test around line 750 ("background successor's alert must stay unread until the user views the tab", plus the selected-tab leg) -- this is the strongest existing guard on the pass being scoped to the selected tab
- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateIpcTests.swift -- paneFocusClearsTargetPaneAlertsInFocusMode -- the IPC route through navigateToPane
- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateSessionEventTests.swift -- the four tests that set `model.isAppActive = false` and then raise bells; they prove the pass does not wipe a background-raised alert

**Tests that will need updating.** Expect these; they assert the thing being changed.

- (likely none, but verify) -- no existing test appears to assert that a focus change *while the app is inactive* clears alerts, which is the one behavior the isAppActive gate removes. `.appBecameActive`'s tests set isAppActive = false and then send the activate Msg, which sets it true first. The UpdateSessionEventTests inactive tests never move focus afterwards. Run the DanTermCore suite once early and treat any red test here as the signal that the isAppActive gate is a real behavior change rather than a free one.
- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateAlertTests.swift -- the fifteen-odd tests that set `alertClearMode = .manual` are unaffected by construction, but one of them (around the .goToMostRecentAlertPane arms) sets manual mode specifically to stop the focus path from interfering; re-read those before assuming they are untouched.

**Write this test first.** Suite: lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateTabTests.swift. Name: "closing the selected tab clears the fallback tab's focused-pane alert in focus mode". Scenario: `var model = makeModel(); model.config.alertClearMode = .focus`; create tab A and tab B in one group; insert an unread `AlertModel(kind: .bell, paneId: tabA.paneTree.focusedPaneId, isUnread: true)`; `update(&model, .selectTab(id: tabB.id))`; then `update(&model, .closeTab(id: tabB.id))`, which makes tab A the fallback selection. Assert `model.selectedTabId == tabA.id` and `model.alerts.allSatisfy { !$0.isUnread }`. Why it fails today: `Update.swift#closeTabRemoval` picks the fallback with a bare `model.selectedTabId = newId` and carries no `markAlertsReadForPane` -- it is the one selection-changing path that never got a copy of the two lines -- so tab A's pane keeps its unread badge, while reaching the same tab through `.selectTab` clears it. This is the real defect the Vetted note found, and the reconcile-in-defer fix makes it disappear by construction. Write a second test in the same commit for the invariant itself: with focus mode on and the app active, after `.movePaneToTab`, `.focusDirection`, and a last-pane `.closePane` that moves focus, assert no unread alert survives on the selected tab's focused pane -- that one passes today and is the regression net for deleting the nine copies.

**Blockers and surprises.** Four. First, the isAppActive gate is a deliberate behavior change and the audit flags it twice: today `.paneBecameFirstResponder`, `.focusDirection` and `applySelectTab` clear alerts whether or not the app is active, and after the fix a background IPC `pane.focus` or `tab.select` would leave the badge lit until the app is foregrounded. That changes what the dock badge shows and needs the user's assent. Second, the good news the finding does not price: both alert-raising helpers -- the `.sessionBell` arm and `#desktopAlertCommands` -- already return early when `model.isAppActive && selectedTab.paneTree.focusedPaneId == paneId`, and they are the *only* two `model.alerts.insert` sites in the whole core, so an idempotent repair pass cannot wipe a freshly raised alert on the focused pane. That is what makes the pass safe to run on every message. Third, ordering inside the defer: `reconcileTabState` can rewrite `selectedTabId` (that is exactly the `closeTabRemoval` fallback path), so the alert pass must come after it. Fourth, `markAlertsReadForPane` is `private` to Update.swift while its natural home beside `reconcileTabState` is ModelOperations.swift -- one of the two has to move, and `scripts/core-purity-lint.sh` plus the layering rules in docs/design/2026-05-28-pure-core-support-split.md govern where. The `.movePaneToTab` / `.movePaneToNewTab` "disagreement" the original evidence claimed is not real -- `PaneTree.adopt` sets `focusedPaneId` to the adopted pane -- so do not write a test asserting a bug there.

**Readiness: needs-decision.** A human must decide whether the `isAppActive` gate is acceptable. Today a focus change clears the focused pane's alerts even while DanTerm is in the background (an IPC `pane.focus` or `tab.select` from a script, for instance); with the gate, that badge survives until the user foregrounds the app. Everything else in this kit is ready, and the `closeTabRemoval` defect it fixes is real and testable today. If the user says the gate is unacceptable, the pass can drop `isAppActive` -- but then `.appBecameActive`'s copy no longer falls out for free and the `.sessionBell` inactive path needs re-checking, since a bell raised on the focused pane while inactive would be cleared by the very next message.

</details>

<a id="reduce-4"></a>

##### REDUCE-4. Derive terminal focus from the model instead of emitting focusSession(false) from four arms

`structural` &middot; impact 3, confidence 3 &middot; effort medium &middot; wave 4 &middot; rewritten

**Files.** `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Command.swift#Command`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#update`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#applySelectTab`, `app/AppRuntime.swift`, `app/PaneFocusReconciliation.swift#reconcilePaneFocus`

**Problem.** Which session is focused is a projection of `selectedTabId` plus that tab's `focusedPaneId`, yet only half of it is pushed, from four copies of the same loop, and only the `false` half. Nothing emits `focused: true`; that half arrives from AppKit responder callbacks. So one fact has two owners and four writers, and an arm that changes the selection without copying the loop silently leaves a background pane believing it has focus.

**Evidence.** `commands.append(.focusSession(paneId: oldPaneId, focused: false))` inside `for oldPaneId in paneIdsForTab(oldTabId, in: model)` appears verbatim four times: in `.createTab`, `.movePaneToTab`, `.movePaneToNewTab`, and `applySelectTab`. `AppRuntime.perform` maps the command to `paneSession(for: paneId)?.setFocused(focused)`, which is `forwardFocusIfChanged`, the same private helper `becomeFirstResponder`/`resignFirstResponder` call with `true`/`false`. The app already owns a model-derived focus pass, `reconcilePaneFocus`, built on `desiredPaneFocus(in: model)`.

**Ideal fix.** Add a `reconcileSessionFocus` pass beside `reconcilePaneFocus` that computes the desired focused pane from the model (`selectedTab.paneTree.focusedPaneId`, and nothing when no tab is selected) and calls `setFocused` on the diff against what it last applied. Delete `Command.focusSession` and all four copies of the defocus loop. `forwardFocusIfChanged` already dedupes, so an idempotent pass costs nothing.

**By construction.** A background pane that still reports focus to its child process becomes unrepresentable: focus is recomputed from the model on every sweep, so no arm can omit the defocus and no ordering can leave two panes focused at once.

**Cheaper fallback.** Keep the command but emit it from one helper called by every arm that writes `selectedTabId`, so at least the four copies collapse into one. The fact still has two owners and the `true` half still comes from AppKit.

**Verification.** Behavioral test at the runtime level (`just test-ui`): split a tab, switch to another tab, and assert the previously focused pane's session reports unfocused; switch back and assert it reports focused again. At the reducer level, assert `.selectTab` returns no commands at all once the projection owns focus.

**Risk.** Focus reporting is externally visible (DECSET 1004 focus events reach the child), so the pass must not thrash: it needs a last-applied cache and must run after `reconcileContainers` has mounted or unmounted the views.

**Vetted.** The four verbatim `commands.append(.focusSession(paneId: oldPaneId, focused: false))` loops are there (`.createTab`, `.movePaneToTab`, `.movePaneToNewTab`, `applySelectTab`), `AppRuntime` maps the command to `setFocused`, and `SwiftTerminalSessionView#forwardFocusIfChanged` is the shared, deduping writer that `becomeFirstResponder`/`resignFirstResponder` also call. The split is deliberate and commented -- `becomeFirstResponder` says "Presentation only. A responder gain is not a model fact" -- so the `true` half comes from AppKit on purpose. I could not find an arm that changes the selection and leaves a live background pane reporting focus: `closeTabRemoval` skips the loop but destroys those panes. So this is structure, not a live defect, which is why I moved confidence down. More importantly the stated fix is wrong in one detail that would break behavior.

**Correction.** The pass must be built on the existing `Projections.swift#desiredPaneFocus`, not on `selectedTab.paneTree.focusedPaneId` alone. When `searchState[paneId].focusOwner == .field` the desired target is `.searchField(paneId)` and the terminal view has resigned first responder, so it reports `focused: false` to the child today; a pass keyed on the focused *pane* would push `true` and start reporting focus to the child while the caret is in the find field -- an externally visible change, since DECSET 1004 events reach the process. So: `reconcileSessionFocus` should call `setFocused(true)` only for a `.terminal(paneId)` target and `false` for every other mounted session, diffed against a last-applied cache and run after `reconcileContainers`.

**Sharper ideal.** If the point is one owner for the fact, the pass should own both halves and `forwardFocusIfChanged`'s calls from `becomeFirstResponder`/`resignFirstResponder` should go too. Keeping the AppKit-driven `true` leaves exactly the two-owner shape the finding names as the problem; what it costs is that a responder change AppKit makes on its own (a click) reports focus one reconcile sweep later rather than instantly, which is invisible at human latency because the click already routes through a Msg.

**Conflicts with.** [LOOKUP-4](#lookup-4)

<a id="reduce-5"></a>

##### REDUCE-5. Raise every pane alert through one function instead of duplicating the ritual in .sessionBell

`simplification` &middot; impact 3, confidence 5 &middot; effort small &middot; wave 2 &middot; confirmed

**Files.** `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#update`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#desktopAlertCommands`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#throttledNotification`

**Problem.** There are two implementations of "raise one pane alert": the `.sessionBell` arm and `desktopAlertCommands`. They repeat the same five steps in the same order, including the one-unread-per-pane hack and the 100-item cap magic number, and they have already drifted -- only one of them applies the terminal metadata length bound.

**Evidence.** `.sessionBell` runs: the `model.isAppActive && focusedPaneId == paneId` skip, `guard tabForPane(paneId, in: model) != nil`, `markAlertsReadForPane`, `AlertModel(... kind: .bell ...)`, `model.alerts.insert(alert, at: 0)`, `if model.alerts.count > 100 { model.alerts.removeLast() }`, then `throttledNotification`. `desktopAlertCommands` runs the identical sequence with `kind: .desktopNotification`, and additionally opens with `guard senderTitle.fitsTerminalMetadataValueLimit, body.fitsTerminalMetadataValueLimit`. The bell path's body is a pane title that never passes through that bound.

**Ideal fix.** Extract one `raiseAlert(model:&, paneId:, kind:, presentation:, body:, env:)` holding the skip rules, the mark-read hack, the insert, the cap (as one named constant on `AppModel`), and the throttle call. `.sessionBell` supplies `.bell` with the pane title; `desktopAlertCommands` supplies `.desktopNotification` with the resolved presentation. The metadata bound stays where the sender's text enters, at the `.sessionNotification` arm.

**By construction.** The alert list can no longer grow past its cap, or skip the mark-read hack, on a path someone adds later: there is one place that inserts an alert, so a third alert kind inherits the whole policy instead of re-stating four of its five steps.

**Cheaper fallback.** None -- the ideal fix is small.

**Verification.** Behavioral tests already pinning the bell path (focused-pane suppression while active, one unread per pane, the 1-second per-kind throttle) must pass unchanged, and the same three assertions must hold for `.sessionNotification`.

**Risk.** Low. The only semantic decision is where the metadata length bound sits; keeping it at the `.sessionNotification` arm preserves today's behavior exactly.

**Vetted.** Read `case .sessionBell` and `desktopAlertCommands` side by side. They run the identical five steps in the identical order -- the `model.isAppActive && focusedPaneId == paneId` skip, `guard tabForPane(paneId, in: model) != nil`, `markAlertsReadForPane`, `AlertModel` + `model.alerts.insert(alert, at: 0)`, `if model.alerts.count > 100 { model.alerts.removeLast() }`, then `throttledNotification`. The drift is exactly as claimed: `fitsTerminalMetadataValueLimit` appears only in `desktopAlertCommands` (grep across lib/ and app/ finds no other production caller), so the bell's body -- the OSC-set pane title -- reaches the alert list and the notification unbounded. The extraction is clean and the 100 cap is a bare literal at both sites.

<a id="reduce-6"></a>

##### REDUCE-6. Tie a pending IPC input request to its pane so pane teardown can reject it

`correctness` &middot; impact 2, confidence 4 &middot; effort small &middot; wave 1 &middot; rescored

**Files.** `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Model.swift#PendingInputRequest`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#rejectPendingCreation`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#closeTabRemoval`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#closePaneBody`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/IpcDispatch.swift`

**Problem.** The reducer treats the two kinds of in-flight IPC work asymmetrically. A pending session creation records enough to be rejected when its pane dies, and every close path does reject it. A pending input request records only its outstanding submission ids, so no close path can find it, and the only thing that ever fails it is app shutdown. A caller whose pane closes mid-delivery waits for the app to quit.

**Evidence.** `struct PendingInputRequest { var remaining: Set<InputSubmissionId> }` -- no pane. `rejectPendingCreation` resolves `model.pane(paneId)?.session?.id` and removes from `pendingSessionCreations`, and is called from `closeTabRemoval`, `closePaneBody`, `deleteGroupBody`, and the `.sessionCreationFailed` arm; there is no counterpart for `pendingInputRequests`. Outside `.inputSubmissionCompleted`, the only writer that clears them is `case .runtimeWillShutdown`, which fails them with "application shut down before pane input was delivered".

**Ideal fix.** Add `let paneId: PaneId` to `PendingInputRequest` (the dispatch site in IpcDispatch already has it in hand) and extend the existing per-pane rejection helper to fail every request owned by that pane with `-32603` when the pane leaves the tree, at the same four call sites that already reject pending creations. Delete the submission ids from `pendingInputSubmissions` in the same step.

**By construction.** A pending input request that outlives the pane it targets stops being representable: every path that removes a pane from the tree can see, and must answer, the requests bound to it -- the same guarantee pending session creations already have.

**Cheaper fallback.** Leave the model as is and rely on the runtime always invoking the completion -- `TerminalPaneSession.send` does reject synchronously when already torn down. That leaves the guarantee outside the core, unprovable by a reducer test, and silent if a send is in flight across teardown.

**Verification.** Reducer test: dispatch a pane input request that leaves a submission outstanding, then send `.closePane` for that pane; assert an `.ipcError` for the request id is returned and `model.pendingInputRequests` is empty. A late `.inputSubmissionCompleted` for the same submission must then produce no second reply.

**Risk.** Must not double-reply: the arm has to remove the request before emitting the error so a completion arriving afterwards finds nothing, which the existing `removeValue` guard in `.inputSubmissionCompleted` already handles.

**Vetted.** `Model.swift#PendingInputRequest` is `var remaining: Set<InputSubmissionId>` with no pane, `rejectPendingCreation` has no counterpart for input requests, and `.runtimeWillShutdown` is indeed the only non-completion writer that clears them -- all as stated. But the stated symptom ("a caller whose pane closes mid-delivery waits for the app to quit") does not survive reading the runtime. `AppRuntime.perform` answers `.sendText`/`.sendInputText`/`.sendInputKey`/`.sendInputWheel` with `send(.inputSubmissionCompleted(id:result:.rejected))` when `paneSession(for:)` is nil, `TerminalPaneSession#send` rejects synchronously with `.rejected(.processEnded)` once `isTornDown`, and `TerminalPTYHost#send` calls the completion with `.rejected(.processEnded)` when `weak self` is gone. So every path I could trace does reply. The value left is the asymmetry itself and making the guarantee provable inside the reducer, which is worth less than impact 3.

**Do after.** [MODEL-6](#model-6)

**Conflicts with.** [MODEL-6](#model-6)

**Current shape.** `struct PendingInputRequest: Equatable { var remaining: Set<InputSubmissionId> }` in `Model.swift` carries no pane. The pane-scoped rejection helper is `Update.swift#rejectPendingCreation(for paneId: PaneId, in model: inout AppModel, message: String) -> [Command]`, which resolves `model.pane(paneId)?.session?.id`, removes from `pendingSessionCreations`, and returns one `.ipcError(reqId:code:-32603,message:)`. It is called from exactly four places, always before the pane leaves the tree: the per-pane loop in the `case .sessionCreationFailed` arm, `deleteGroupBody`, `closePaneBody` (the non-emptied branch -- the emptied branch delegates to `closeTabRemoval`, which rejects per pane itself), and `closeTabRemoval`. Pending input requests have no such counterpart: outside `case .inputSubmissionCompleted`, the only writer that clears them is `case .runtimeWillShutdown`. The dispatch site, `IpcDispatch.swift#dispatch` `case .paneInput(let paneId, let input)`, already has the pane id in hand and has already run `try requirePane(paneId, in: model)`.

**Change sites.**

- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Model.swift#PendingInputRequest` -- Add `let paneId: PaneId` -- or, taking MODEL-6's sharper ideal, delete this struct and make the single map `[InputSubmissionId: PendingInputSubmission]` with `requestId` and `paneId` on the value.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/IpcDispatch.swift (`case .paneInput` in `dispatch`)` -- Record `paneId` alongside the submission ids.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#rejectPendingCreation` -- Extend (and rename, e.g. `rejectPendingIpcWork(for:in:)`) so it also fails every input request owned by that pane with `-32603` and deletes those submissions from the map. Remove the request/submissions before appending the error so a late `.inputSubmissionCompleted` finds nothing -- the existing `removeValue` guard in that arm then makes the second reply impossible.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift (`case .sessionCreationFailed`, per-pane loop)` -- Call site keeps its shape; message text for the input half should say the pane's process failed to start.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#deleteGroupBody` -- Same call site, now also rejecting input requests.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#closePaneBody` -- Same call site. Note the emptied-tree branch returns through `closeTabRemoval` before reaching this line, so the tab path must cover the last-pane case -- it does, because it loops every pane id.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#closeTabRemoval` -- Same call site, per pane in the tab.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift (`case .runtimeWillShutdown`)` -- Unchanged in intent, but must keep emitting one error per request, not per submission, if the map shape changes with MODEL-6.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateSessionEventTests.swift#runtimeShutdownRejectsEveryPendingPaneEffect` -- Constructs `PendingInputRequest(remaining: [submissionId])` with no pane; stops compiling the moment the struct gains a field. Reseed it through a real `pane.input` dispatch.

I also checked `movePaneToTab` / `movePaneToNewTab`, which move a pane without destroying it and therefore correctly need no rejection. The list should be complete._

**Tests that must keep passing.** These are the safety net.

- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateIpcTests.swift -- UpdateIpcTests, "pane.input defers success until every submission is delivered" -- the happy path must still reply exactly once, on the last delivery.
- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateIpcTests.swift -- UpdateIpcTests, "pane.input rejects once when any submission is undeliverable" -- one error, and a later completion for a sibling submission stays silent. This is the no-double-reply guard the new rejection path must not break.
- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateSessionEventTests.swift -- "runtime shutdown rejects pending creation and input requests" -- shutdown still fails both kinds of pending work.
- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateAlertTests.swift and UpdateSearchTests.swift -- the closePane / closeTab / sessionCreationFailed / deleteGroup cleanup tests -- they pin that the four teardown paths keep doing everything else they already do.

**Tests that will need updating.** Expect these; they assert the thing being changed.

- lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateSessionEventTests.swift -- "runtime shutdown rejects pending creation and input requests" -- the only test that builds a `PendingInputRequest` by hand. Adding `paneId` (or replacing the struct) breaks its construction and its `model.pendingInputRequests.isEmpty` assertion.

**Write this test first.** Suite: `UpdateIpcTests` in lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/UpdateIpcTests.swift. Name: "pane.input in flight is rejected when its pane closes". Scenario: `makeModel()`, `createTab(&model)`, then `update(&model, .splitFocusedPane(direction: .horizontal))` so the tab has two panes and closing one neither empties the tab nor quits the app. Take `paneId = selectedTab(in: model)!.paneTree.focusedPaneId`, dispatch a `pane.input` request with a two-item `input` array (matching the existing multi-submission tests) under a known `requestId`, collect the submission ids off the emitted `.sendInputText` / `.sendInputKey` commands, and complete none of them. Then `let closed = update(&model, .closePane(paneId: paneId))`. Assert (a) `closed` contains an `.ipcError(reqId: requestId, code: -32603, ...)`, and (b) a following `update(&model, .inputSubmissionCompleted(id: submissions[0], result: .delivered))` returns an empty command list -- no second reply. Why it fails today: nothing in `closePaneBody` or its helpers looks at `pendingInputRequests`; only `rejectPendingCreation` runs, which touches `pendingSessionCreations` only. So (a) fails -- the close emits no `.ipcError` for the request -- and the request stays in the model until `.runtimeWillShutdown`. Assertion (b) already holds today, which is what makes it the right regression guard for the ordering risk the finding names.

**Blockers and surprises.** The finding's stated symptom does not survive contact with the runtime, and the audit's own vetting says so: `AppRuntime.perform` answers a send to a missing pane with `.inputSubmissionCompleted(... .rejected)`, `TerminalPaneSession#send` rejects synchronously once torn down, and `TerminalPTYHost#send` completes with `.rejected(.processEnded)` when its `weak self` is gone. So no caller actually hangs today; the value is the reducer-provable guarantee and the symmetry with pending session creations. Say that plainly in the plan rather than justifying the work with a hang that cannot happen. Two mechanical notes. The four call sites all run before the pane leaves the tree because `rejectPendingCreation` needs `model.pane(paneId)`; the input half does not need that, so the ordering stays free, but keep the two inside one helper so a fifth teardown path cannot pick up one and miss the other. And `closePaneBody`'s emptied-tree branch returns through `closeTabRemoval` before reaching the rejection line, so verify the last-pane-in-tab case through the tab path -- it loops every pane id, so it is covered, but a test that closes the only pane of a tab exercises a different line than the split case. The sequencing note from MODEL-6 applies here too: the two findings cite each other as prerequisites, and the clean resolution is to do them as one change built on MODEL-6's single-map shape.

**The preparer's read on the ideal fix.** The ideal is right but under-specified in one place worth deciding up front: `PendingInputRequest` gaining a `paneId` and MODEL-6 deleting `PendingInputRequest` are the same four sites twice. Do the combined shape -- one `[InputSubmissionId: PendingInputSubmission]` carrying `requestId` and `paneId` -- and both findings close in one pass. Also, the plan should not lead with the "caller waits for the app to quit" symptom, which the runtime disproves.

**Readiness: ready.** An agent can start on this from the above.

##### REDUCE-7. Delete the senderless .markAlertRead message

`simplification` &middot; impact 2, confidence 5 &middot; effort small &middot; wave 6 &middot; confirmed

**Files.** `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Msg.swift#Msg`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Update.swift#update`

**Problem.** `Msg.markAlertRead` has no producer anywhere in the app, the iOS target, or the IPC dispatch table. Its only callers are two unit tests, so the reducer arm and the test both describe a path the product cannot take, and a reader has to check the whole tree to learn that.

**Evidence.** Grepping `markAlertRead` across app/, ios/, and lib/ outside tests returns only the declaration in `Msg.swift` and the arm in `Update.swift`; the alerts popover row activation sends `.activateAlert`, and bulk clearing goes through `.markAllAlertsRead`, `.clearAlertsForPane`, and `.clearAlertsForTabs`. The two hits in `UpdateAlertTests.swift` are the only senders.

**Ideal fix.** Remove the case, the arm, and the two tests that exercise it. If per-alert acknowledgement is wanted in manual clear mode, add it back with the UI or IPC producer in the same change so the vocabulary always names something a user can do.

**By construction.** n/a -- this removes dead vocabulary rather than making a state unrepresentable.

**Cheaper fallback.** None -- the ideal fix is small.

**Verification.** The build fails if any real producer existed; `swift test --package-path lib/DanTermCore` passes after the two tests are deleted, and the remaining alert tests still pin `.activateAlert` marking its alert read outside manual mode.

**Risk.** None beyond losing a path nothing uses; the same behavior is reachable through `.activateAlert` and the bulk-clear messages.

**Vetted.** Grepped `markAlertRead` across lib/, app/, ios/, and integrations/. Exactly four hits: the case in `Msg.swift`, the arm in `Update.swift`, and two sends in `UpdateAlertTests.swift`. No IPC method dispatches it, no menu or popover sends it. Dead vocabulary, and the removal is mechanical.

#### Area: Core model and projections (`MODEL`)

_Scope: Pure domain model and derived projections (lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore: Model.swift, ModelOperations.swift, PaneLayout.swift, PaneGridOverride.swift, Projections.swift, PaneRosterProjection.swift, DisplayLine.swift, DropZone.swift, DragDropInput.swift, EntityTitle.swift, SidebarItemStore.swift, ScrollbarMath.swift, ChipKind.swift)_

**The auditor's read on the area.** The core of this area is in good shape: `PaneTree` already makes "a pane with no owning leaf" unrepresentable, `PaneGridOverride` fails instead of clamping, `DisplayLine` is a genuinely tight boundary type, and `PaneLayout` is a clean pure projection with one rounding rule shared by layout and drag inversion. The remaining defects all have the same shape -- a product type whose fields are only valid in certain combinations, or a second copy of a fact some other value already carries. I did not audit Update.swift, IpcDispatch.swift, Persistence.swift, PaneLifecycleReducer.swift, Reconcile.swift, or SidebarView.swift as subjects; I read them only to establish reachability and call-site counts for defects whose home is in my files. I looked at ScrollbarMath's UInt64 subtraction (`total - offset - len` traps on underflow) and dropped it: the engine's `scrollProjection` guarantees `topRow + windowRows <= totalRows`, so I could not show it reachable.

<a id="model-1"></a>

##### MODEL-1. Replace PendingConfirmation's subject-plus-optional-payloads with one per-subject enum

`structural` &middot; impact 3, confidence 5 &middot; effort medium &middot; wave 1 &middot; rewritten

**Files.** `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Model.swift#PendingConfirmation`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Projections.swift#desiredConfirmation`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/ModelOperations.swift#closeConfirmationCopy`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/ModelOperations.swift#emitConfirmation`

**Problem.** `PendingConfirmation` stores a `ConfirmationSubject` next to four independently-optional payload fields (`tabTitle`, `impact`, `deleteGroup`, `quitAuthorized`). Only five of the many field combinations are legal, and the pairing is enforced nowhere -- it is a convention shared by three construction sites and re-checked defensively at every read. The type admits `.deleteGroup` with a nil `deleteGroup`, `.tab` with a nil `tabTitle`, and `.app` with a frozen `impact`.

**Evidence.** `PendingConfirmation` declares `let subject: ConfirmationSubject; let tabTitle: DisplayLine?; let impact: CloseImpact?; let deleteGroup: DeleteGroupConfirmation?; let quitAuthorized: Bool`. Every arm of `desiredConfirmation` re-derives the pairing defensively -- `case .pane: guard let impact = pending.impact else { return nil }`; `case .tab(let tabId): guard tabById(...) != nil, let tabTitle = pending.tabTitle, let impact = pending.impact else { return nil }`; `case .deleteGroup: guard let frozen = pending.deleteGroup ... else { return nil }`. `closeConfirmationCopy` carries two crash arms that exist only because the type permits the combination: `case .app: preconditionFailure("app confirmations do not have frozen close copy")` and `case .deleteGroup: preconditionFailure("delete-group confirmations do not have close copy")`. `emitConfirmation` hand-fills the nils per subject (`tabTitle: nil, impact: nil, deleteGroup: nil, quitAuthorized: false` for `.app`), and `Update.swift#emitDeleteGroupConfirmation` fills a different subset.

**Ideal fix.** Delete the subject/payload split and give `PendingConfirmation` an `id` plus one enum whose cases carry exactly their own data: `.quit`, `.closePane(PaneId, CloseImpact, quitAuthorized: Bool)`, `.closeTab(TabId, title: DisplayLine, CloseImpact, quitAuthorized: Bool)`, `.closeTabs([TabId], CloseImpact, quitAuthorized: Bool)`, `.deleteGroup(GroupId, DeleteGroupConfirmation)`. `desiredConfirmation` then returns a non-optional projection for a non-nil pending confirmation, and `closeConfirmationCopy` takes only the three close cases and loses both `preconditionFailure` arms. `ConfirmationSubject`, which confirm dispatch still wants, becomes a computed property.

**By construction.** A pending confirmation missing the payload its subject requires, or carrying a payload its subject has no use for, becomes unrepresentable; so does a confirmation kind with no close copy reaching `closeConfirmationCopy`, which deletes both `preconditionFailure` calls rather than guarding them.

**Cheaper fallback.** none -- the ideal fix is a mechanical retype of one value plus three construction sites and one reader.

**Verification.** DanTermCore test: for each confirmation the reducer can raise (close pane, close tab, close multiple tabs, quit, delete group), assert `desiredConfirmation(in: model)` is non-nil right after the raising message and that `.confirmConfirmation(id:)` performs the action. Today the tab arm can project nil, which orders the panel out (`Reconcile.swift#reconcileConfirmation` calls `confirmationPanel?.orderOut(nil)`) while `model.pendingConfirmation` stays set -- a transaction the user can never answer.

**Risk.** Confirm/cancel dispatch in Update.swift switches on `subject`; keep a computed `subject` through the change so those arms are untouched.

**Vetted.** Read `Model.swift#PendingConfirmation`, `ModelOperations.swift#emitConfirmation`, `#closeConfirmationCopy`, `Projections.swift#desiredConfirmation`, and the confirm/reconcile arms in `Update.swift`. Every quote is exact: the five stored fields, the two `preconditionFailure` arms, the per-arm `guard let impact` re-derivation, and the hand-filled nils. The type genuinely admits `.deleteGroup` with a nil `deleteGroup` and `.tab` with a nil `tabTitle`. Two claims in the write-up are wrong: `Update.swift#reconcilePendingConfirmation` runs in the `defer` of every `update()` and clears the pending confirmation when the subject tab, pane, tab list, or group stops being live, so the "transaction the user can never answer" the Verification section describes is already prevented; and `desiredConfirmation` cannot become non-optional, because the `.tab` and `.deleteGroup` arms also consult the live model (`tabById`, `model.groups.first`) and must keep returning nil for a subject that has just died.

**Correction.** `PendingConfirmation` pairs a `ConfirmationSubject` with four independently-optional payload fields, so only five of the representable combinations are legal and the pairing is a convention shared by three construction sites (`emitConfirmation`'s two branches and `Update.swift#emitDeleteGroupConfirmation`). The cost is paid at every read: each arm of `desiredConfirmation` re-derives the pairing with a defensive `guard`, and `closeConfirmationCopy` carries two `preconditionFailure` arms that exist only because the type permits subjects it has no copy for. The ideal fix is unchanged -- one enum whose cases carry exactly their own data, with `subject` as a computed property for the dispatch arms -- but state the payoff accurately: it deletes four optionals, three defensive guards and both `preconditionFailure` calls. It does not make `desiredConfirmation` total, because that function must still return nil for a subject whose tab or group has left the model, and it fixes no live bug: `reconcilePendingConfirmation` already retracts a confirmation whose subject dies. Verification should assert the projection is non-nil right after each raising message and that `.confirmConfirmation(id:)` performs the action -- not that a stranded panel exists today.

**Conflicts with.** [CHROME-2](#chrome-2)

**Current shape.** `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Model.swift#PendingConfirmation` is a struct with five stored lets: `id: ConfirmationId`, `subject: ConfirmationSubject`, `tabTitle: DisplayLine?`, `impact: CloseImpact?`, `deleteGroup: DeleteGroupConfirmation?`, `quitAuthorized: Bool`. `ConfirmationSubject` (same file) is `case pane(PaneId) / tab(TabId) / tabs([TabId]) / deleteGroup(GroupId) / app`. Two production sites construct the value: `ModelOperations.swift#emitConfirmation(_ model: inout AppModel, subject: ConfirmationSubject, quitAuthorized: Bool = false, env: CoreEnv) -> [Command]` (an `.app` branch that fills every payload with nil/false, and a close branch that fills `impact` plus `tabTitle` only for `.tab`) and `Update.swift#emitDeleteGroupConfirmation(_ model: inout AppModel, groupId: GroupId, env: CoreEnv)` (fills `deleteGroup`, nils the rest). `Projections.swift#desiredConfirmation(in model: AppModel) -> ConfirmationProjection?` switches on `pending.subject` and re-derives the pairing with a `guard let impact` / `guard let tabTitle` / `guard let frozen` per arm. `ModelOperations.swift#closeConfirmationCopy(subject: ConfirmationSubject, impact: CloseImpact, quitAuthorized: Bool) -> CloseConfirmationCopy` carries `preconditionFailure` arms for `.app` and `.deleteGroup`. Every quote in the finding still matches the tree exactly; nothing has moved.

**Write this test first.** No new failing test. This is a pure retype: the audit's own Vetted and Correction paragraphs state that `Update.swift#reconcilePendingConfirmation` already retracts a confirmation whose subject dies, so the "stranded panel" the original Verification described does not exist today and no behavior changes. The characterization test is `lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/CloseConfirmationTests.swift` -- "confirmation projection follows every pending subject", which drives `.requestCloseTab` and `.requestQuit` through the real reducer and asserts the exact projected id, title, informative text, command list, and confirm title for both. Pair it with `UpdateGroupTests`' delete-group arm (title "Delete group \"Work\"?", confirm "Move to General", secondary "Close Tabs") to cover the fifth kind, and with "confirmation retracts when its subject dies and survives unrelated changes" to pin the retraction rule the guards were standing in for. If the implementer wants one new behavioral test rather than none, the honest one is a coverage gap rather than a bug: no single test today asserts that every one of the five raising messages yields a non-nil `desiredConfirmation` and that `.confirmConfirmation(id:)` then performs the action. Write that as a table-driven test in `CloseConfirmationTests` BEFORE the refactor -- it passes on the current tree, so it is a characterization test, and it must be stated as such rather than dressed up as red.

**Blockers and surprises.** Three things to know. (1) `ConfirmationSubject` cannot simply be deleted: `closeImpact(for:in:)`, `closeSubjectHasGrown`, `reconcilePendingConfirmation`, and every confirm/cancel dispatch arm switch on it. Keeping it as a computed property on `PendingConfirmation` is what makes this a contained change -- the audit's Risk paragraph says exactly this and it holds. (2) `desiredConfirmation` cannot become total. The `.closeTab` arm still calls `tabById` and the `.deleteGroup` arm still calls `model.groups.first` twice, and both must keep returning nil for a subject that died between the reducer and the projection. Anyone who reads the finding's original Ideal-fix line ("returns a non-optional projection") and tries to deliver it will fight the model; the Correction already retracts it. (3) CHROME-2 is marked "Do after MODEL-2" and touches `ConfirmationProjection` (adding a typed answer per button) rather than `PendingConfirmation`, so it does not collide with this work -- but it does change the same `desiredConfirmation` function body. If both land in the same week, do MODEL-1 first: it reshapes the input side, CHROME-2 reshapes the output side, and doing them in that order means CHROME-2 writes its answer enum against the already-clean switch. Nothing in `app/` reads `PendingConfirmation` at all (`app/Reconcile.swift#reconcileConfirmation` and `app/ConfirmationPanel.swift` see only `ConfirmationProjection`), and `Persistence.swift` never touches it -- the blast radius really is core plus core tests. No public `lib/` API ripple: `DanTermCore` compiles same-module into the app via the tracked symlink, and none of these symbols are `public`.

**Readiness: ready.** An agent can start on this from the above.

<a id="model-2"></a>

##### MODEL-2. Make SidebarItemStore reject nothing, or report rejection, so a dropped row op cannot strand the outline

`correctness` &middot; impact 2, confidence 3 &middot; effort medium &middot; wave 1 &middot; rewritten

**Files.** `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/SidebarItemStore.swift#SidebarItemStore`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Projections.swift#advanceSidebarCache`, `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Projections.swift#computeSidebarRowOps`

**Problem.** `SidebarItemStore.apply` validates every index and cache lookup itself and returns `.none` when a check fails. `.none` also means "this op legitimately produced no outline work", so the caller cannot tell a rejected structural op from a no-op -- and the reconcile driver advances its projection cache to `new` regardless. A single rejected insert or remove desynchronizes the mounted outline from the projection permanently: the next sweep diffs against a cache that claims the op landed, so nothing ever emits the repair and no path escalates to `reloadAll`.

**Evidence.** `apply` has eight fail-closed guards returning `.none`, e.g. `case .insertTab: guard let parent = groupItemCache[groupId], var children = childItems[groupId], children.indices.contains(index) || index == children.count else { return .none }` and `case .removeGroup(let index): guard !projection.isSingleGroupMode, rootItems.indices.contains(index), case .group(let group) = rootItems[index].kind else { return .none }`. The consumer `app/SidebarView.swift#applyRowOp` does `switch store.apply(op, projection: projection) { case .none: return ... }` and reports nothing back, while `app/SidebarReconcileDriver.swift` unconditionally stores the result of `advanceSidebarCache(...)`. `advanceSidebarCache` retains only rows named by `suppressedRenameTarget`, `unappliedTabIds`, or `unappliedGroupIds`, and only `.repaint`/`.setGroupCollapsed` ever populate those sets -- never a rejected insert or remove. Indices are cumulative (`computeSidebarRowOps` documents "each index is relative to the running (intermediate) state"), so one rejection invalidates every later index in the script.

**Ideal fix.** Stop validating indices in the store: have it apply each op against the projection it is handed, deriving the row position from that projection's own ordering, so an out-of-range or unknown-parent op is unrepresentable and `apply` becomes total. Where a rejection genuinely cannot be designed away, widen the return so it names rejection -- `enum SidebarOutlineMutation { case noWork; case rejected; ... }` -- and have the driver turn any `rejected` into a `reloadAll` in the same sweep while keeping the old projection in its cache.

**By construction.** "The mounted outline disagrees with the last-applied projection, and the diff can never notice" stops being expressible: either the store cannot reject an op the diff produced, or the cache cannot advance past a rejection.

**Cheaper fallback.** Keep the guards but return `.rejected` and treat it as a forced rebuild. The store can still disagree with the projection, but the damage is bounded to one extra reload instead of a permanently wrong outline.

**Verification.** Pure test over the diff/store pair: build old and new `SidebarProjection`s, run `computeSidebarRowOps`, apply the script to a `SidebarItemStore` seeded from a stale state (one row already missing), and assert the store's resulting row ids equal `new`'s row ids. Today ops are silently dropped and the assertion fails.

**Risk.** Deriving indices from the projection changes the store's contract with `app/SidebarView.swift#applyRowOp`, which feeds NSOutlineView index-based insert/remove calls; those calls must receive the same index the store used, so the mutation must keep carrying it.

**Vetted.** Read all of `SidebarItemStore.swift`, `Projections.swift#computeSidebarRowOps` / `#advanceSidebarCache` / `#guardSidebarRenameOps`, `app/SidebarView.swift#applyRowOp`, and `app/SidebarReconcileDriver.swift#reconcile`. The nine `return .none` guards, the `.none: return` in the executor, and the unconditional cache advance are all exactly as quoted. But I could not substantiate the stated damage. The cache the diff runs against is `advanceSidebarCache`'s output, which only ever rolls back group and tab *attribute* fields, never row identity or order, so the store's structure and the cached projection cannot diverge through the normal path -- the guards are dead in every sequence I could construct. The one asymmetry I did find is different from the one the finding names: `computeSidebarRowOps` emits `insertGroup`/`removeGroup` unconditionally, while the store refuses both when `projection.isSingleGroupMode`. Reaching it needs the single group's *id* to change between two sweeps, which needs a create-group plus a delete-group coalesced into one sweep -- and even then the surviving tab rows carry the same ids in the same order, so the visible outline stays correct.

**Correction.** The real defect is narrower than "a dropped row op strands the outline": it is that one rule -- "in single-group mode there are no group rows" -- is stated in `SidebarItemStore.apply` as a silent rejection and is not stated in `computeSidebarRowOps` at all, which emits group insert/remove ops in that mode anyway. Nobody has shown a sequence where that rejection produces a wrong outline, so this is hazard removal, not a bug fix. Two things are worth doing and both are small: gate the group-level `sidebarSequenceOps` call on `!new.isSingleGroupMode` (or return `.reloadAll` when the single group's id changes), so the diff and the store agree about what a group row is; and widen the store's return so rejection is nameable -- `.rejected` -- with the driver turning it into a `reloadAll` and keeping the old projection in its cache. Drop the proposed verification, which seeds the store from a state the pipeline cannot produce and therefore proves nothing about live behavior; test the single-group group-identity change end to end instead.

**Conflicts with.** [RECON-4](#recon-4)

<summary><b>Starter kit</b> -- current shape, 10 change sites, the tests, and the first failing test</summary>

**Current shape.** `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/SidebarItemStore.swift#SidebarItemStore` is a struct holding `tabItemCache: [TabId: SidebarItem]`, `groupItemCache: [GroupId: SidebarItem]`, `rootItems: [SidebarItem]`, `childItems: [GroupId: [SidebarItem]]`. Its single-op entry point is `mutating func apply(_ op: SidebarRowOp, projection: SidebarProjection) -> SidebarOutlineMutation`, and `SidebarOutlineMutation` is `case none / reloadAll(groupCollapseStates:) / insert(item:at:inParent:groupCollapseState:) / remove(item:at:inParent:) / setGroupCollapsed(item:collapsed:) / repaint(item:)`. Fourteen `return .none` guards are spread across the eight op arms. The producer is `Projections.swift#computeSidebarRowOps(old: SidebarProjection?, new: SidebarProjection) -> [SidebarRowOp]`, which rebuilds wholesale only when `old` is nil or `old.isSingleGroupMode != new.isSingleGroupMode`, and otherwise emits group-level ops from `sidebarSequenceOps` unconditionally -- including in single-group mode, where the store refuses every one of them. The consumers are `app/SidebarView.swift#applyRowOp` (switches on the mutation, `case .none: return`) reached from `app/SidebarView.swift#applySidebarOps(_:projection:renameTargetToEnd:) -> (tabs: Set<TabId>, groups: Set<GroupId>)`, and `app/SidebarReconcileDriver.swift#reconcile(_:tally:in:) -> SidebarReconcileResult`, which unconditionally assigns `appliedProjection = advanceSidebarCache(...)`. Every quote in the finding matches the tree; nothing has moved.

**Change sites.**

- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/Projections.swift#computeSidebarRowOps` -- The primary fix. Gate the group-level `sidebarSequenceOps` call on `!new.isSingleGroupMode`, and add the missing rebuild trigger: when both sides are single-group mode but `old.groups.first?.id != new.groups.first?.id`, return `[.reloadAll]`. Without the second half, gating alone leaves a single-group identity change emitting no ops at all and the outline keeps the dead group's tabs.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/SidebarItemStore.swift#SidebarOutlineMutation` -- Add a `case rejected` so a refused op is nameable and distinct from `.none` ("this op legitimately did no outline work").
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/SidebarItemStore.swift#SidebarItemStore.apply(_:projection:)` -- Every one of the fourteen `return .none` guard exits becomes `return .rejected`. The two `.reloadGroup` / `.reloadTab` arms are the judgement call: `updateGroupItem`/`updateTabItem` returning nil means the projection has no such row, which is a genuine disagreement -- treat it as `.rejected` too, and leave `.none` unused by any guard.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Sources/DanTermCore/SidebarItemStore.swift#SidebarItemStore.apply(_:projection:) (the array overload)` -- The `[SidebarRowOp]` script convenience discards each result. Either leave it (it is documented as a test convenience) or have it surface "any op was rejected" so the store tests can assert on it directly.
- `app/SidebarView.swift#applyRowOp` -- Add a `case .rejected` arm and report it upward. Currently the function returns Void and accumulates through two `inout Set` parameters; the simplest shape is a third `inout Bool didReject`.
- `app/SidebarView.swift#applySidebarOps` -- Signature widens: return `(tabs: Set<TabId>, groups: Set<GroupId>, rejected: Bool)` (or a small struct). On rejection the view must also run the repair -- feed `.reloadAll` through the store and call `rebuildAllRows(groupCollapseStates:)` -- before the selection restore block, or the outline stays wrong for the rest of the sweep.
- `app/SidebarReconcileDriver.swift#reconcile(_:tally:in:)` -- On a rejected sweep, do not advance the cache: keep `appliedProjection` at its prior value so the next sweep re-diffs, or (if the view performed the reloadAll repair) set it to `newProjection` directly, skipping `advanceSidebarCache`'s retention entirely since a full rebuild painted everything. Pick one and write it down -- the two are not interchangeable.
- `app/SidebarReconcileDriver.swift#SidebarReconcileResult` -- If UI tests need to observe the escalation, add a `rejected` or `didReloadAll` field. Optional, but it is the only way a tests-ui test can assert the escalation happened rather than inferring it from row contents.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/SidebarItemStoreTests.swift#isNoOutlineMutation (file-private helper)` -- Currently `if case .none = mutation { return true }`. Rename/retarget to `isRejectedOutlineMutation`, matching `.rejected`.
- `lib/DanTermCore/Tests/DanTermCoreTests/SidebarItemStoreTests.swift#rejectedRowOpsReturnNoneWithoutChangingStore` -- Its twelve-op table plus the two wrong-mode ops all assert `.none` today. They must assert `.rejected` instead. The test name changes with it.
